512455|2026-09.headline: Lloyds Metals H1 FY27 record: revenue INR9,545 crore (+94% YoY), EBITDA margin 38.33% (+542 bps), PAT INR2,639 crore (+113%).
512455|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue rose 62% YoY to INR4,132 crore and EBITDA rose 83% to INR1,538 crore, with a 37.22% margin (+419 bps). Management attributes the margin gains to the slurry pipeline cutting iron ore freight, higher realisations and a richer mix of value-added products such as pellets, which now make up 61% of standalone revenue. Thriveni's Q2 was weaker on monsoon disruption and higher diesel and explosives costs, with pass-through negotiations under way. Management guided to ~INR13,000 crore capex for FY27, and the Chemaf debt restructuring is targeted for closure within 3 to 4 months. Copper FY27 target was cut to 5,850 tonnes from 8,000 tonnes because of Surya Mines feed and sulphuric acid constraints.

segments.name: Iron ore (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 production 3.95 Mt (+15.5% YoY) and sales 2.12 Mt; H1 production 10 Mt (+35%). Realisation ~INR670/t, EBITDA INR2,082/t in Q2 (INR2,239/t H1). Monthly run rate above 2 Mt.

segments.name: DRI and power
segments.commentary: Q2 DRI sales 160.6 kt (+81% YoY); H1 343.1 kt (+104%). DRI realisation INR31,040/t with EBITDA INR9,231/t in Q2. Power volumes +82% in Q2 and +85% in H1.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Q2 production 2.11 Mt; H1 3.81 Mt after second plant commissioned in May. Realisation INR11,348/t in Q2 (INR11,520/t H1); EBITDA INR4,604/t in Q2 (INR4,988/t H1). Sales mix 71% domestic, 29% export.

segments.name: Thriveni (MDO, mining)
segments.commentary: H1 iron ore volume 30.31 Mt including BHQ and coal 44.84 million cubic metres including overburden. Q2 margins were hit by rain and fuel and explosives costs; management says pass-through is being negotiated with clients.

guidance_outlook: FY27 iron ore volume expected at about 8 Mt, rising to about 9.5 Mt in FY28, as the 20% add-on takes capacity from 8 Mt to 9.6 Mt over the next 3 to 4 months.
Capex guided at about INR13,000 crore for FY27 (H1 INR6,000 crore) and around INR10,000 crore or more in FY28.
Wire rod steel plant: blast furnace and coke oven to start in Q4 FY27, steel plant and wire rod mill in Q1 CY2027, a quarter later than earlier planned.
Beneficiation volumes expected from FY29; usable iron ore stays at 26 Mt through the period.
Chemaf debt restructuring expected to close within 3 to 4 months, before the end of FY27. Long-run Chemaf net debt guided to about $500 million from about $800 million today.
Copper FY27 target cut to 5,850 t from 8,000 t. Chemaf plants targeted for production in FY28.
Management expects H2 volumes to rise in Lloyds Metals and the MDO business, with DRI operations strong. Copper is expected to be slower in H2.
Management indicated about 38% margin for both H1 and H2 at standalone level.
capex_capacity: Pellets: both 4 Mt plants running above rated capacity; debottlenecking under way and a third pellet plant being added.

Steel: 1.2 Mt integrated plant (wire rod) progressing toward commissioning. Separately, a 3 Mt steel plan has 1,200 acres of land and a 4.5 Mt EC; only the captive power plant has started, and the configuration study is due in a couple of months.
Slurry pipeline: first line at full capacity; a longer, larger network is planned to carry beneficiated material.
Chemaf: Etoile and Mutoshi copper-cobalt complexes targeted at 74,000 t copper and 20,000 t cobalt a year at full potential, with completion targeted by FY27 end and production in FY28.

Thriveni: Western Hill has 88 electric units operating and 20 more at the rail siding; 14 mobile crushers and 26 heavy earthmoving units mobilised for BHQ. Gold plan approved for 1.5 Mtpa mining and processing at Thriveni Lloyds Swarnagiri.
demand_pricing: Management says iron ore pricing is set internally based on end-product market, stocks and order book, and sees INR6,700/t as sustainable.
Copper pricing cited at about $14,500/t.
Sulphuric acid shortage in DRC is raising Surya Mines costs; diesel in DRC is about $3.2/litre, roughly 3x India.
Thriveni cost pressure from higher HSD and explosives prices after the West Asia crisis; pass-through to clients under negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is iron ore realisation above benchmark, and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no specific Indian benchmark and that INR6,700/t reflects quality; it believes pricing can sustain. It says 26 Mt of ore is available to 2051, and it is not expanding downstream beyond ore availability.

qa_highlights.question: When will Chemaf debt restructuring complete and what is the net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Closure targeted within 3 to 4 months, before FY27 end. Net debt is guided to about $500 million long-run from about $800 million, including capex debt. Consolidation is full, with 51% of profit going to minority interest.

qa_highlights.question: Thriveni margin dip in Q2 and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the rainy season in Odisha and Jharkhand, plus higher fuel and explosives costs. Pass-through to NTPC-linked mine owners is being implemented, and management does not foresee missing its EBITDA projections.

qa_highlights.question: Tata Steel MDO scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Work is via BRPL, a Tata Steel and Lloyds JV, with equipment rented to it. Expected 12-14 Mt iron ore and 1.5-1.8 Mt manganese from next year; rates not yet final. Joda West manganese began at small scale, with a fuller ramp from December.

qa_highlights.question: Copper FY27 target: 8,000 t on slide 15 or 5,850 t on slide 20?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is now 5,850 t for FY27. The cut reflects Surya Mines challenges and a focus on completing Chemaf. Third-party ore processing is less lucrative, so ramp-up is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Funding: borrowings and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the standalone borrowing plan is about INR9,500 crore, with debt-to-equity targeted at 60-65% (below 75%). Net debt is within 1x to 1.5x forward 12-month EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 weakness and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is seasonally weak due to monsoon and cost pressure, but management says standalone margins are steady at about 37-38% across H1 and H2. Volumes are expected to rise in H2.

risks_watch: Surya Mines copper output is constrained by sulphuric acid availability and cost, and by third-party ore; FY27 copper target is 5,850 t.
Chemaf restructuring (target 3 to 4 months) and its debt at about $800 million, with minority dilution of 51%.
Steel plant commissioning slipped about a quarter; blast furnace and coke oven start in Q4 FY27.
Thriveni margin pass-through on fuel and explosives costs is still under negotiation.
Chemaf PNG (Panguna) project is at an early stage with no agreement signed and no volume or cost projections.
$300 million NCD enabling resolution in place; use of proceeds not defined beyond capex.
Consolidated net debt below INR20,000 crore, with standalone net debt INR9,316 crore.
512455|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on standalone margins and H1 records, and evasive on specifics (Panguna, the copper target and the hypothetical war impact). Management was cautious on Surya Mines and copper near-term execution. Management answered the Q2 seasonality and Thriveni questions with clear explanations.
key_quotes: the first half of FY27 has been the best H1 in the company's history, record revenue, record EBITDA and record PAT on both a stand-alone and a consolidated basis
This is a structural re-rating of the earnings base, not a cyclical spike.
We are not chasing volume for its own sake. We are building a business that is structurally advantaged and built to last.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided standalone margin of about 38% for both H1 and H2, after Q2 at 37.22% (+419 bps YoY), with slurry pipeline cutting freight and pellets at 61% of standalone revenue, though Thriveni pass-through is still under negotiation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 20% add-on takes iron ore capacity from 8 Mt to 9.6 Mt in 3 to 4 months, the Chemaf complexes are under construction for FY28 production, and the wire rod steel plant starts blast furnace in Q4 FY27 and steel/wire rod mill in Q1 CY2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 iron ore volume guided at about 8 Mt against H1 production of 10 Mt (+35%) and a monthly run rate above 2 Mt, with DRI sales up 104% in H1 and H2 volumes expected to rise; copper is the exception, cut to 5,850 t.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is guided at about INR13,000 crore (H1 INR6,052 crore) and about INR10,000 crore or more in FY28, and a 3 Mt steel configuration study is due in a couple of months with 1,200 acres of land already held.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Copper FY27 target was cut from 8,000 t to 5,850 t, Chemaf production is pushed to FY28, and steel commissioning slipped about a quarter, so the guidance direction is mixed rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Copper is already cut and Surya Mines is constrained by sulphuric acid, Thriveni pass-through is unresolved after the Q2 margin hit, and the steel plant slipped a quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The wire rod steel plant (1.2 Mt integrated) starts blast furnace and coke oven in Q4 FY27 and steel plant and wire rod mill in Q1 CY2027, but it has already slipped a quarter and no product volumes are guided.

rows.label: Chemaf debt restructuring closure
rows.why: Management targets closure before FY27 end, with long-run Chemaf net debt guided to about $500 million from about $800 million today.

rows.label: Chemaf copper-cobalt production
rows.why: Etoile and Mutoshi are targeted at 74,000 t copper and 20,000 t cobalt a year at full potential, with completion by FY27 end and production in FY28, but FY27 copper is cut to 5,850 t.

rows.label: Tata Steel MDO scope via BRPL
rows.why: Expected 12-14 Mt iron ore and 1.5-1.8 Mt manganese from next year, but rates are not yet final.

tone.note: Management was confident on standalone margins at about 38% and H1 records, and cautious on Surya Mines, copper execution and Thriveni pass-through; analysts pushed on the iron ore realisation sustainability, the copper target cut and Thriveni's Q2 dip.

512529|2026-03.headline: Viyash Q4 FY26 revenue INR920 crore (+19.1% YoY), adjusted EBITDA about INR200 crore at 21.7% margin; FY26 PAT INR225 crore.
512529|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was described by management as the strongest quarter in company history, the first full 12-month results of the combined Viyash-SeQuent entity. Revenue rose 19.1% YoY to INR920 crore, with formulations up 28% to INR499 crore and APIs up 5% to about INR384 crore. Adjusted EBITDA rose about 64% to INR200 crore and PBT swung from a INR37 crore loss to a INR125 crore profit. FY26 revenue was INR3,420 crore (+13.8%), adjusted EBITDA INR702 crore (+59.6%), and PAT INR225 crore versus INR16 crore in FY25. Management also cited a credit rating upgrade to AA- (long-term) and A1+ (short-term).

financial_highlights.value: INR125 crore PBT / INR66 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR37 crore PBT and loss of INR32 crore PAT in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR349 crore PBT / INR225 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PBT more than 26x; PAT more than 14x vs INR16 crore

segments.name: Animal Health formulations
segments.commentary: All regions growing strongly per management. Animal health business moved from a flat INR350 crore plus or minus INR10 crore over five years to a INR400 crore run rate this year. Companion animal platform build-out is planned for FY27 with a Boehringer Ingelheim distribution partnership.

segments.name: Human health formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 formulations up 28% YoY. Shift toward complex products and internalised APIs; a dedicated potent oncology lab in R&D is being readied this quarter or next. US subsidiary (60% owned) revenue about INR400-425 crore.

segments.name: API and CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 API revenue up 8% to INR1,491 crore; Q4 API up 5%. Management deliberately cut low-margin intermediates. Life cycle management CDMO business with 8-10 innovators is about INR200-225 crore and is expected to grow about 40% in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 life cycle management (innovator) CDMO business expected to grow about 40% from a base of about INR200-225 crore.
Management expects comfortable double-digit API growth next year, roughly in line with formulations growth.
Management sees 15% annual growth as possible over the next five years; a detailed strategy and investor meeting are planned, possibly in June.
Revenue target of INR1,000 crore EBITDA stated, with timing to be confirmed at the investor meeting; management earlier cited INR800 crore for FY27 or FY28.
Synergies accrued at about INR50-60 crore annualised, with a target of INR125-150 crore annualised over the next 12-18 months.
Tax rate to be modelled at about 27% for FY27 and FY28, moving to 26-27% after one-off merger-related adjustments roll off.
Goodwill amortisation to fall to about INR35 crore in FY27 from about INR100 crore in FY26; depreciation excluding this to stay similar to FY26.
EBITDA margins expected to be maintained, but FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs.
Management is evaluating selective inorganic opportunities and options to buy out minority stakes (Spain option by 2028).
capex_capacity: Manufacturing expansion in Spain and debottlenecking at the Turkey manufacturing site are underway.
Capex approved for R&D expansion; companion animal R&D to expand 5-6x, targeting 7-8 products per year, with R&D hiring starting over the next six months.
Capex for capacity increase in Viyash has been invested and is awaiting approval, which management expects to bring further synergies.
Two high-potent dedicated API facilities; API batch capability ranges from 0.5-1 kg up to 100 kg.
API R&D team of about 250 scientists including analytical and process; human health formulation R&D about 55-60 scientists.
demand_pricing: Animal health: about 70-80% of API volumes go to innovators; generics pricing falls to about 60-70% of innovator price versus 10-15% in human generics.
Companion animal addressable market in Europe about $1 billion (excluding vaccines); India companion animal market a few hundred crore.
Formulation model is partnership-based, with development paid by partners and profit share typically 50:50 (customers cited include Cipla and Dr. Reddy's).

Raw material and freight: impact in March was immaterial; freight added INR1-2 crore in Q4; solvent costs were the main pressure. Price increases are being used to offset, with key materials stocked for 1-2 quarters.
Commodity intermediate margins are about 30-35%; management is exiting these in favour of APIs and formulations.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the CDMO business and how will it scale over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the life cycle management CDMO business is about INR200 crore with 8-10 big innovators, and 90%-plus of relationships are existing. Ramp-up of NCE Phase III CDMO work takes years.

qa_highlights.question: Which subsidiaries drive minority interest, and how big are they?
qa_highlights.answer: Viyash owns 60% of the US formulations business (revenue about INR400-425 crore) and 60% of the Spain business (FY26 revenue about INR550 crore). Minorities account for about 20% of PAT; Spain buy-back option exists by 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Animal health growth priorities and Boehringer Ingelheim partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on API for patent expiries from 2028 onwards (15-20 products identified, 5-6 large), geography expansion for large animal products, and companion animals with the BI distribution deal and 7-8 new products per year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability versus pure-play API peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects gross margins to hold at current levels, plus or minus 1-2%, through forward and backward integration and dropping commodity products. Margin gains beyond that are expected only with CDMO scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables growth and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose mostly with revenue; days increased by only about 5-6 days in Q4. Focus is on converting EBITDA into PAT, with a tax regime shift for some subsidiaries from 34-35% to 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material and geopolitical impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Impact began in March and was not material; key materials are stocked for 1-2 quarters and price increases are being used to offset solvent and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is API growth single digit and when will it turn double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intermediates were cut deliberately; quality API and animal health APIs are growing double digit, and FY27 should see comfortable double-digit API growth with more approvals.

risks_watch: Investment year in FY27 (R&D, pre-operating costs) may dilute EBITDA margins despite management's margin-maintenance guidance.
Raw material cost volatility (solvents, freight) linked to geopolitical disruption; management says price increases can offset only for now.
Receivables growth outpacing revenue in some geographies (e.g. Turkey) with long credit periods; EBITDA-to-PAT conversion remains a stated focus.
Synergy realisation (INR50-60 crore run-rate versus INR125-150 crore target) depends on approvals taking 12-18 months.
US companion animal generic guidance is complex (BA/BE requirements), delaying the planned US entry.
Minority interest (about 20% of PAT) and the Spain buy-back timeline.
512529|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and integration, with a clear focus on execution. Management was less precise on specific numbers (e.g. revising the INR1,000 crore EBITDA target timing and asking for later confirmation at an investor meeting), and it deferred detailed strategy until a planned June meeting.
key_quotes: Q4 FY '26 is the strongest quarter in the company history. EBITDA surpasses INR200 crores.
We are able to take it to INR400 crores run rate.
Whatever we are doing this year, I can expect next year at least 30%, 40% growing innovator business.
Yes, 15% definitely quite possible. Still, we are working on the detailed strategy.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects gross margin to hold within plus or minus 1-2% of the 55.1% Q4 level, and FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs, so EBITDA margin expansion beyond the 21.7% Q4 level is not guided; gains depend on CDMO scale-up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spain manufacturing expansion and Turkey debottlenecking are under way, and a Viyash capacity capex is approved and awaiting clearance, but no capacity sizes or dates were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides comfortable double-digit API growth in FY27 (vs +8% in FY26 and +5% in Q4), with the life-cycle management CDMO business (INR200-225 crore base) expected to grow about 40%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex has been cleared for R&D (companion animal R&D to expand 5-6x) and the Viyash capacity capex is awaiting approval, with a strategy and investor meeting planned for June, so a further capex update is probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 59.6% to INR702 crore and Q4 PAT swung to INR66 crore, but management has not raised numbers and is only pointing to a INR1,000 crore EBITDA ambition with timing still to be confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs, and solvent and freight costs add pressure (freight INR1-2 crore in Q4), though price increases and 1-2 quarters of stocked materials are offsetting for now.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Companion animal platform with Boehringer Ingelheim is planned for FY27 with 7-8 new products per year targeted, and an oncology potent lab in R&D is being readied this quarter or next.

rows.label: US companion animal generic entry
rows.why: US entry is planned but delayed by complex BA/BE requirements, with no timeline given.

rows.label: Spain minority buy-out option by 2028
rows.why: Minorities hold about 20% of PAT and the Spain (60% owned, FY26 revenue about INR550 crore) buy-back option exists by 2028; management is evaluating selective inorganic options.

rows.label: Synergy ramp to INR125-150 crore annualised
rows.why: Synergies are accruing at INR50-60 crore annualised today, and the target is INR125-150 crore, dependent on approvals taking 12-18 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on integration, Q4 record quarter and FY27 API and CDMO growth, but cautious on the margin investment year, raw material pressure, and vague on the INR1,000 crore EBITDA target timing; analysts' questions focused on API growth being single digit, receivables and EBITDA-to-PA

512529|2026-06.headline: Viyash Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 946 crore, EBITDA margin expanded to 21.6% (up ~530 bps) and PAT more than doubled to Rs 79 crore.
512529|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 946 crore (up 19.5% YoY, 2.9% QoQ), with EBITDA of Rs 205 crore and margin of 21.6% versus 16.2% a year earlier. PAT of Rs 79 crore is after about Rs 19 crore of incremental ESOP cost tied to the post-amalgamation grant. Net debt fell to Rs 86 crore (0.1x EBITDA), and management said the Sequent-Viyash integration is complete. Human API revenue was flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material price volatility, which management expects to reverse in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs 51.9% in Q1 FY26 (~+220 bps YoY)
vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 (~+530 bps YoY)
vs Rs 20.4 crore in Q1 FY26
Net debt/EBITDA 0.1x vs 0.24x last quarter, ~1x a year ago

financial_highlights.value: Rs 25 crore total, of which Rs 19 crore incremental
financial_highlights.change: Grant of 1.3 crore options, 2.8% of post-amalgamation paid-up capital

segments.name: US (Human formulation)
segments.commentary: Grew about 60% per management (about 45% YoY and 6% QoQ in USD per analyst); Rs 126 crore of Q1 revenue is Human formulation. Management said 60% growth will not repeat, but growth is stable, with a 50-55% US market share.

segments.name: Europe (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Reported roughly 13% growth; analyst computed EUR 16.8 million flat YoY in constant currency. Management guided full-year Europe growth of 18-20% INR, citing phasing across quarters.

segments.name: Emerging markets (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% (about 23% in USD per analyst); volume growth was 25%, led by Turkey, Brazil and Mexico. Management said 25% volume growth will not be sustained every quarter.

segments.name: Animal Health India domestic
segments.commentary: Grew about 60%; management plans to expand field force and portfolio.

segments.name: API (Human and Animal)
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material volatility. Animal API run-rate about Rs 100 crore, with Vizag capacity commercialised from July. API is about 40-45% of total revenue, roughly two-thirds Human and one-third Animal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to be the best quarter in company history for API, citing a rebound in orders after customers delayed purchases in June.
FY27 double-digit growth, with management citing 13-15% overall (Human API 13-14%, Animal Health 20%+).
Europe growth of 18-20% INR for the full year; Europe double-digit growth in FY27 excluding FX.
ESOP cost of about Rs 150 crore for FY27 (Rs 25 crore in Q1, about Rs 40 crore per quarter thereafter), falling to Rs 25-30 crore in FY28.
Depreciation plus goodwill amortisation of Rs 25 crore per quarter; drops to about Rs 10-11 crore in Q2, and management expects about Rs 15 crore benefit per quarter from Q3 onward.
Minority interest expected at about 16-17% of total profit; minority stakes in the US and Spain to be fully acquired within 1-2 years.
Capex of Rs 250-300 crore per year; companion animal tablet capacity targeted to be ready by January-February 2027.
Bio For Life (Italy) acquisition SPA signed; closing expected in the next few months and within FY27. Bigger revenue expected after 18-24 months.

Human high-potent oncology first product expected in 2029; majority of new product revenue after 2030. Management targets Rs 1 billion (~Rs 10,000 crore?) aspiration by 2032 implying 18% CAGR from FY27 base.
capex_capacity: Companion animal tablet manufacturing: design finalised, construction to start within weeks, target completion January-February 2027 for exhibit batches.
High-potent formulation development lab completed last week; three high-potent API modules built over last 18-24 months.
Albendazole capacity expanded; US approval received for Vizag site, commercialisation started from July 2026.
R&D ramped up for companion animal products; equipment ordered and people hired.
Annual capex of Rs 250-300 crore, described as modest relative to existing business.
demand_pricing: Human API demand deferred in June as customers waited for raw material/solvent prices to stabilise; management says orders are returning after July.
Management noted it raised prices when raw material costs rose and may reduce them if solvent prices fall.
Human high-potent and oncology products expected to face 50-60% price erosion at generic entry versus 95% for general APIs, per management.
Target market share for new products: 10-15% on average, with 25-30% in best cases.
Europe: Spain performing strongly; Benelux and other countries lagging in tenders. Europe volume and pricing are the main growth drivers.
Animal Health portfolio focus shifted to differentiated products; the company has stopped developing mature commodity products.

qa_highlights.question: Naman Bagrecha (IIFL): Europe revenue looks flat YoY on a constant-currency basis; what is driving this and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe grew about 13% and computed EUR 16.8 million versus EUR 16.8 million in Q1 FY26 was disputed in the exchange; Rajaram Narayanan said full-year Europe growth should be close to 18-20% in INR, with Q1 phasing tied to tenders and contract timing, and Q3 typically the peak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging markets grew about 23% in USD; what drove it and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth led by Turkey, Brazil and Mexico with volume up 25%; management said volume growth will not run at 25% every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: US business grew about 45% YoY and 6% QoQ in USD; what drove it and is the margin improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited restructuring: moving volume products to India, vertical integration of some products with in-house API, new launches and higher R&D revenue; 60% growth will not repeat but growth is stable with 50-55% market share; management expects the margin improvement to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why was API flat QoQ, and what is the Animal API revenue run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers delayed June purchases while waiting for raw material and solvent prices to settle after the war; management said orders returned after July and Q2 would be the best API quarter in company history. Animal API run-rate is about Rs 100 crore, with Vizag Albendazole capacity commercialised from July.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi (Monarch Networth): Can API growth exceed 20% for several quarters, and what is the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided Animal Health above 20% and overall FY27 growth of 13-15%, with Human API 13-14%; big Human launches are expected later, from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP cost trajectory and what are the Q2-Q4 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ESOP cost was about Rs 25 crore including Rs 19 crore incremental; about Rs 40 crore per quarter for Q2-Q4, about Rs 150 crore for FY27, falling to Rs 25-30 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Sheth (Quest): How big is the high-potent oncology business and what is the pipeline and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capability was built over 18-24 months with three API modules and a high-potent formulation lab completed last week; first formulation product expected in 2029, majority of revenue after 2030; at least 5-6 APIs filed and at least 50% of portfolio is first-to-file or first-to-launch.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and goodwill amortisation and interest cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation plus goodwill amortisation was Rs 25 crore in Q1; about Rs 10-11 crore in Q2, with about Rs 15 crore per quarter benefit from Q3. Management is restructuring interest, including Ireland debt, after the Sequent India debt restructuring last year.

qa_highlights.question: Chintan Sheth (Greek Capital): What is the minority interest outlook and the Human vs Animal split?
qa_highlights.answer: Minority interest was about 17% in Q1 and about 20% for FY26; management guided 16-17% of total profit going forward. Minority stakes in the US and Spain to be bought out within 1-2 years. US formulation is the only Human formulation (Rs 126 crore of Rs 554 crore), and API is about 40-45% of revenue, roughly two-thirds Human.

qa_highlights.question: Kumar Saurabh (Scientific Investing): What is the opportunity size and market share target for first-to-file APIs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said generic price erosion is about 95% for general APIs and 50-60% for oncology/high-potent; target market share is 10-15% on average, with 25-30% in best cases; the 2032 Rs 1,000 crore aspiration implies about 18% CAGR from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Mehul (40 Cents): How much will BioForLife add to revenue, and how much is API in revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bigger revenue comes after 18-24 months, with 25-30% growth expected after FY28-29; API is about 40-45% of revenue, roughly two-thirds Human and one-third Animal.

risks_watch: Europe growth phasing: Q1 EU reported growth was about 13% and management guided 18-20% INR for FY27; Benelux and other countries lag in tenders.

513097|2026-09.headline: Shivalik H1FY27: consolidated revenue up ~39%, EBITDA up 48%, PAT up 40%, driven by core components and value-add conversion.
513097|2026-09.overview: Management said H1FY27 revenue grew about 39%, EBITDA 48% and PAT 40%, with growth led mainly by previously sampled core-component developments moving into regular business rather than by PCBA or CCS assemblies. Shunt volumes fell about 16% as customers shifted from wide strip to finished components, while value rose about 36% in shunts; management said commodity pass-through explains part of the value increase, with underlying volume-led growth of about 25-26%. Management outlined an assembly (busbar/PCBA) opportunity of INR 100-200 crore at a 15-16% EBITDA margin versus 26-27% for legacy lines, and a 3-4x revenue scale-up over a multi-year horizon with blended EBITDA moving toward 20-22%. No quantitative FY27 guidance was given; the call was mostly qualitative.

qa_highlights.question: Is the current quarterly run-rate sustainable, and what is the demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developments convert into sticky, staggered business; growth is expected to continue for a few years, though timing of new developments can be uneven.

qa_highlights.question: Why did shunt volume fall ~16% while value rose ~36%?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers previously bought wide strip for their own resistor production; that has dropped and SBCL now ships finished resistors with more processes. Commodity pass-through explains part of value growth; underlying volume-led growth is 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US shunt revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Some US customers now receive supply directly for end users outside the US, mainly in Asia; some US demand resumed in the last 2-3 months, partly offset elsewhere.

qa_highlights.question: Will inorganic opportunities change capital allocation after the dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend does not materially affect funds; free cash is sufficient, and acquisition opportunities are expected to come in staggered stages rather than requiring immediate capital.

513228|2026-03.headline: Pennar Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14.91% to INR41.04 crores on total income of INR933.7 crores; management commits to 20% PAT growth in FY27.
513228|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 2.26% to INR933.7 crores while EBITDA grew 15.27% to INR114 crores and PAT grew 14.91% to INR41.04 crores, with PAT margin at 4.44% versus 3.9%. FY26 was a record year: total income INR3,666 crores (up 12.33%), PAT INR138.83 crores (up 16.22%), PAT margin 3.83% versus 3.7%. Management attributed the Q4 revenue slowdown to revenue slipping into Q1 and a solar hit in diversified engineering, and blamed labour shortages for PEB India underperformance in FY26. Working capital rose to 82 days, and gross debt-to-equity rose to 0.98x, both of which management is targeting to reduce.

513262|2026-09.headline: Steel Strips Wheels Q2 FY27 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR1,930 crore and standalone EBITDA per wheel hit INR404, with management reiterating the figure as sustainable.
513262|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the strongest quarter in company history, with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT. Standalone EBITDA including other income rose 107% YoY to INR237 crore, margin 12.3% vs 9.6%, and PAT rose 209% to INR119 crore. Management attributed the gains to richer aluminium mix, cost optimisation, higher exports and customer price revisions for non-raw-material input costs. A supplementary invoicing of INR140 crore in Q2 (INR183 crore in H1) relating to raw-material pass-through was disputed by analysts as flattering EBITDA; management said it has no bearing on EBITDA. The board also approved a greenfield plant at Sambhajinagar (INR1,400 crore over 60 months) and an interim dividend of INR1.50 per share.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Highest growth among segments in Q2 across domestic and export markets; domestic steel wheel demand up 28% in H1 per management. Management expects record CV sales in October.

segments.commentary: Market share rose to 45% from 43%; tractor volume up about 15% in H1 per management.

segments.name: Aluminium knuckles
segments.commentary: Progressing in line with expectations; seeking more customer approvals. Commercial production expected in Q4 FY27 at Bhuj with 1.1 million units annual capacity.

513349|2026-03.headline: Ajmera Realty FY26 presales hit record INR 1,701 Cr (+57% YoY), beating INR 1,600 Cr guidance; FY27 presales target set at INR 2,200 Cr.
513349|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year for Ajmera Realty: presales of INR 1,701 Cr (+57% YoY), collections of INR 1,103 Cr (+71%), and total sales revenue of INR 1,098 Cr (+46%). EBITDA rose 25% to INR 306 Cr and PAT rose 24% to INR 157 Cr. Debt-to-equity fell to 0.53x against an annual guidance of 0.85x. Management guided FY27 presales to about INR 2,200 Cr and debt-to-equity to 1.00x, citing the Kanjurmarg land conversion, a planned INR 1,800 Cr of business development, and eight launches. Most Q&A focused on the Kanjurmarg conversion timeline, Versova luxury sales pace, Manhattan pricing, and the reason for the higher gearing guidance.

513349|2026-06.headline: Ajmera Realty Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR320 crores, PAT up 14% to INR45 crores, debt cut to INR680 crores.

Ajmera Solis entered revenue recognition for the first time this quarter. Debt fell by INR57 crores to INR680 crores, taking debt-equity to 0.47x. Sales value was INR146 crores against collections of about INR173 crores, and INR89 crores was received from a property asset monetisation against a INR330 crores target.

513349|2026-09.headline: Ajmera Realty Q2 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR320 crore and PAT 55% to INR49 crore; debt cut to INR646 crore.
513349|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 sales were INR224 crore (72,883 sq ft carpet) against collections of INR190 crore, and H1 sales reached INR370 crore. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew strongly YoY, with 33Fifteen (Bandra commercial) recognising revenue for the first time this quarter. Debt fell INR34 crore QoQ to INR646 crore, debt-equity is 0.44x and weighted cost of debt dipped to 10.75%. Management's near-term story rests on about 8 launches (~38 lakh sq ft, ~INR7,000 crore top line) mostly in Q4 FY27, plus the Kanjurmarg 7-acre land conversion, which has slipped repeatedly and drew the most investor pushback.

qa_highlights.question: Kanjurmarg 7-acre tie-up and conversion timing; will conversion happen before 31 Dec before cost rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says conversion is hoped for before 31 Dec but hurdles remain; it is a government process and it declined to quantify the cost if it slips. Commercial talks have not started, though title and approvals have progressed.

qa_highlights.question: Will presales of INR2,200 crore be met given the Q4 launch cluster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of exceeding the target within six months, citing 8 launches and early agent interest. It acknowledged up to one or two launches could slip because approvals are not fully in place.

qa_highlights.question: Balance sheet capacity to fund Wadala commercial plus launches within 6 to 9 months.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO says leverage is 0.44x with room to roughly double, financial closure is in place for Wadala, and Solis collections will accelerate cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability with cost inflation and pricing pressure.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects geopolitics and commodity pressure to normalise and will time launches and sales velocity against cost and pricing elasticity. No margin number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Kanjurmarg timeline visibility and what follows conversion.
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not commit to a timeline. After conversion it expects a 4-5 month routine master plan and approvals step, then a commercial and residential launch together and a 7-acre monetisation or JV.

qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed micro-market competition and redevelopment supply for Vann's slow sales. It said water shortages in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 will be managed through tankers and borewells, and there are no BMC restrictions yet.

513375|2026-03.headline: Carborundum Universal FY26 standalone sales rose 8.6% to INR 3,024 crore, while consolidated PBIT fell 25.3% to INR 404 crore on subsidiary losses.
513375|2026-03.overview: Standalone performance rebounded through H2 FY26, with Q4 sales up 23.1% YoY to INR 845 crore and Q4 PAT more than doubling to INR 122 crore. Consolidated sales crossed INR 5,000 crore (INR 5,149 crore, +6.5%), but consolidated PBT before exceptions fell 27.2% to INR 416 crore, driven by VAW sanctions, Foskor, Awuko and Rhodius losses. Management decided to wind down Awuko and to close Foskor Zirconia, booking exceptional items of INR 135 crore in FY26. FY27 guidance is for about 4-4.5% consolidated sales growth, which falls to 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko, with capex of about INR 400 crore.

segments.name: Standalone Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,270 crore (+6.2%); H1 down 2.8% to INR 594 crore, H2 up 15.6% YoY to INR 675 crore. PBIT INR 195 crore (+0.9%), margin 15.3% vs 16.1%.

segments.name: Standalone Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 906 crore (+11.1%), with exports up 100% to over 33% of sales. PBIT rose 31.1% to INR 82 crore; management said growth was mainly volume with price roughly flat.

segments.name: Standalone Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,000 crore (+6.5%). PBIT fell 8% to INR 214 crore. Wear ceramics de-grew 9%; engineering ceramics grew 30% on SOFC demand; metallized cylinders grew 9% after a H1 production issue.

segments.name: Consolidated Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 2,271 crore (+5.1%); Q4 INR 610 crore (+13.4% YoY). PBIT margin 4.3% vs 7.0%, with Rhodius loss about INR 45 crore and Awuko loss about INR 75 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,632 crore (+3.7%), held back by VAW Russia sales down 35% in roubles. Foskor losses hit PBIT; consolidated segment PBIT INR 91 crore vs INR 177 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,268 crore (+9.3%); reported margin 20.2%. Industrial ceramics INR 569 crore (+7.8%); refractories and anti-corrosives INR 437 crore (+4.7%).

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales EUR 61 million, down 8.8% from EUR 67 million, after about EUR 5 million lost to a Q1 logistics transition. PAT loss EUR 2.6 million vs EUR 0.2 million in FY25.

segments.name: Awuko
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 10.5 million (+4.6%); loss before tax rose to EUR 7.7 million. Voluntary winding-up started in Germany.

segments.name: VAW Russia
segments.commentary: Sales about 6 billion roubles vs 9.4 billion (-35.3%) under US sanctions; profit before tax 617 million roubles vs 1.7 billion, but still profitable.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (South Africa)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 461 million (+11.2%); loss before tax ZAR 77 million vs ZAR 37 million. Operations being discontinued as not commercially viable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated sales growth of about 4-4.5%; about 11-12% excluding Foskor Zirconia and Awuko (together INR 343 crore of FY26 sales).
FY27 standalone Abrasives growth about 12% per management; consolidated Abrasives sales +5.5-6% (11-12% excluding Awuko).
FY27 consolidated Ceramics growth of 15-15.5%; consolidated Electrominerals sales -6.5% to -7% due to Foskor closure (8-9% excluding Foskor).
Margin guidance FY27: Abrasives 9.5-10% (FY26 comparable 7.9%), Ceramics 20.5-21% (reported 20.2%), Electrominerals 9-9.5% (comparable FY26 9.1%).
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore, mainly advanced ceramics for power electronics, brown-fused alumina expansion, a 110 kV substation and a tunnel kiln for refractories.
Rhodius expected to grow sales about 5% in FY27 with a very small loss; Aspiration 2030 targets were not formally quantified.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex FY26 INR 309 crore (standalone INR 235 crore) against INR 350 crore guided earlier.
Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components facility: first module commissioned in H1 FY26 at INR 66 crore; serial supplies start FY27, material revenue expected from 2029.
Aerospace and defence ceramics facility at INR 49 crore; STANAG 4 vehicle armour qualification secured; SCOMET approval awaited.
White fused alumina furnace upgrade from 2 MVA to 4.5 MVA at about INR 53 crore, adding up to INR 95 crore revenue potential; treatment facility INR 30 crore for up to INR 120 crore revenue.
Thin wheel capacity at Hosur using DRONCO-acquired assets: INR 83 crore outlay, 46 million wheels, peak revenue about INR 120 crore.
Refractories fired capacity to rise 75%; metallized cylinder capacity to be expanded in three phases over 18-24 months.
demand_pricing: Standalone H2 FY26 growth was broad-based, with Abrasives, Ceramics and Electrominerals each up double digits sequentially. Management attributed part of the rebound to GST rationalisation and festive demand.
China cut its abrasive export rebate from 9% to 0% from April 2026 (one analyst cited 13%). Management called it good for domestic industry but too recent to show in numbers.
Electrominerals growth was mainly volume; price roughly flat. Chinese import intensity has not declined.

Ceramics growth of 9.3% missed the 13-14% guided earlier, mainly due to deferred projects, especially in the glass segment. Management attributes the 15% FY27 outlook to backlog and customer forecasts.
Over 80% of Ceramics sales are exports; under 10% of Abrasives sales are exports.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the SOFC ceramics business become, and what is the wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give wallet share but said it is an important supplier, with customer visibility to about 2028, and it expects a meaningful share of revenue as the engineered segment grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Ceramics growth miss the 13-14% guidance, and does it signal structural competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed mainly deferred projects, not structural change, and expects the 15% FY27 growth to be backed by backlog and customer forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for semiconductor fab-equipment ceramics revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Material qualification takes four to six years; samples are tested and serial production starts, with material revenue expected from 2029 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to profitability at Rhodius?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects sales growth of 6-7% with the one-time EUR 5 million logistics loss not recurring, plus a special profitability programme, to return it to a small loss or breakeven in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there alternatives to Russian silicon carbide supply from VAW?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said replacing the capacity would be costly and difficult; it awaits sanctions relief and has no alternative for now.

risks_watch: Foskor Zirconia closure needs approvals in South Africa; the Awuko winding-up is ongoing in Germany.
VAW Russia sales are constrained by US sanctions, with no alternative supply route identified.
FY27 consolidated growth of 4-4.5% is low versus the 11-12% comparable figure, so the reported drop from exits needs watching.
Ceramics growth depends on the timing of deferred projects and on the US business, where exports fell 40% in FY26 for wear ceramics.
Rhodius returning to breakeven depends on recovering the lost EUR 5 million in sales and on cost actions.

513375|2026-06.headline: Carborundum Universal Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores; consolidated PAT up 23.4% to INR 76 crores, with Electrominerals up 33%.
513375|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores, broad-based across Electrominerals (+33%), Ceramics (+15.2%) and Abrasives (+14.7%), and were flat QoQ. Standalone PAT was INR 88 crores, up 14.3% on a like-to-like basis excluding a one-time INR 68 crore subsidiary dividend in Q1 FY26. Consolidated PAT of INR 76 crores was helped by a INR 25 crore gain on leasehold transfer at Sterling Abrasives, while Abrasives standalone margins were squeezed by an oil-linked and fuel cost push of about INR 16 crores. Management raised the consolidated Ceramics growth guidance to 23-25% and kept other segment guidance unchanged, while Foskor divestment and Awuko closure updates are now promised for Q2.

segments.name: Electrominerals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 282 crores, +33% YoY and +12.2% QoQ, mainly volume and export-led with very little price increase; PBIT rose to INR 39 crores from INR 7 crores. Exports rose to about 40% of segment sales from about 35% last year.

segments.name: Ceramics (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 274 crores, +15.2% YoY but -1.6% QoQ on refractories seasonality; PBIT INR 59 crores vs INR 62 crores YoY as IC gains were offset by fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.

segments.name: Abrasives (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 328 crores, +14.7% YoY, volume-driven; PBIT INR 34 crores with margin falling to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY, due to about INR 16 crores cost push (resins, oil, fuel) and INR 8-9 crores volume drop QoQ.

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany, Abrasives)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 15.6 million, +18% YoY and +1.1% QoQ (INR 172 crores, +33.9% YoY); loss after tax EUR 0.7 million vs EUR 1.6 million a year ago. FY27 guidance of about 5% growth and a small PAT loss is maintained.

segments.name: CUMI Awuko Abrasives (Germany, being wound up)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 2.89 million, +11.1% YoY; loss after tax EUR 1.69 million vs EUR 0.9 million a year ago. Voluntary winding up is in progress and management aims to complete it in about a quarter.

segments.name: VAW Russia (Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales RUB 1.58 billion, -14.1% YoY in roubles but INR 201 crores, +3.1% YoY in rupee terms; PAT RUB 52.1 million vs RUB 71.5 million a year ago. Business is domestic-focused.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (51% subsidiary, Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 107 million, -14.7% QoQ; deemed commercially unviable. Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed a INR 17 crore loss; divestment or exit options are being explored, targeted for Q2.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth: FY27 guidance of about 4-4.5% reported, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko; management says it could reach about 15% on a comparable basis given the order book.
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth: guidance of 5.5-6% retained; 11-12% excluding Awuko (about INR 108 crores).
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth: raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%; management expects the Ceramics margin to be at the higher end of the guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales: guidance of a 6.5-7% decline retained (reported basis); 8-9% growth excluding Foskor, and management says this could be 9-10%.

Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% retained, with Ceramics 20.5-21% maintained. Q1 consolidated Abrasives margin was about 2.5% excluding the Sterling gain, which management attributes to Awuko losses.
Capex of about INR 400 crores for FY27 retained. Rhodius guidance of about 5% growth with a small PAT loss is unchanged.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex was INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 against INR 64 crores a year earlier; the FY27 target of about INR 400 crores is unchanged, and management would not give project-wise splits.

FY27 capex covers expansion in advanced ceramics for power electronics (including substrates), metallized tubes, rings and brazed assemblies, brown-fused alumina expansion, an integrated furnace for thermal spray powders and a zirconia furnace.
Metallized substrate facility is being set up with one anchor customer and a technology tie-up; it should be commissioned in FY27, with revenue from FY28.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components: small in FY27, picking up in FY28, with a peak targeted for FY30. Aerospace and defence will improve in FY27 with the main ramp from FY28. Powder purity is moving from 5N to 6N.
Refractories capacity expansion is on track, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was volume-driven with very small price increases; management sees early easing of Chinese import competition but says exchange rates and China's export-rebate changes make the trend unclear.
Ceramics: growth was seen across segments; Wear Ceramics returned to growth this quarter after several quarters, and Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics are growing mainly through exports.

Electrominerals: volume-led, with treated-product mix helping margins; little or no price increase. Export share is rising toward 40%, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way.

Abrasives cost push: oil-linked inputs such as resins rose sharply in May and June, with oil reaching about $117 a barrel. Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5%. The US-Iran conflict that began end-February 2026 drove the cost pressure.
Management said it will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, and will decide one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi (Avendus): How much of standalone Abrasives growth is value vs volume, traction by sub-segment, and are Chinese import changes helping share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was predominantly volume-driven with very small price increases. Import competition from China has just started to ease, but management said exchange rates and China's export-benefit withdrawal make the trend unclear; it sees the trend as positive.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi: Where is Ceramics traction strongest across Wear, Technical, Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics, and is Metallized Cylinder/Engineered Ceramics growth domestic or export?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth optimism is across all segments except Wear, which is normal growth; Wear returned to growth this quarter after several quarters. Metallized Cylinder and Engineered Ceramics growth is predominantly export.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit (Equirus): How will semiconductor wafer fab, aerospace/defence and substrate revenues phase across FY27 and FY28, and does the Ceramics guidance upgrade come mainly from SOFC?
qa_highlights.answer: Substrate facility to be set up in FY27 with revenue from FY28; wafer fab components very small in FY27, picking up in FY28 and peaking in FY30; aerospace/defence slightly better in FY27 with main ramp from FY28. The upgrade is a combination of Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders and SOFC Ceramics, with no split given.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: What are plans for zirconia products and Foskor divestment progress, and what drove the Electrominerals volume vs price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has a couple of options after discussions with South African partners and aims to close the Foskor process by Q2; a fuller update is promised then. Electrominerals growth was mostly volume and product mix (treated products), with very little or no price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: Why was Abrasives margin under pressure if Electrominerals prices were not up significantly?
qa_highlights.answer: Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5% and were offset by normal price increases; the pressure came from oil-linked inputs such as resins, which rose sharply in May and June with oil reaching about $117 a barrel, plus fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: Amit Anwani (PL Capital): What is the strategic view on VAW Russia, its utilisation and sales update, and SOFC contribution and volume vs price in the 11-12% comparable guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in Russian business, which remains domestic-focused; management's aim is to stay put, comply with laws and serve the domestic market. Full-year growth is expected to be predominantly volume-driven with normal price increases; no individual SOFC split was shared, and pricing beyond normal will be decided one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Jain (Dolat): Excluding the Sterling gain, consolidated Abrasives margin is about 2.5% versus 9-10% guidance; what is the comment, and what is the CAPEX breakdown and unallocated expense run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is largely Awuko losses, which are still being incurred, so it holds the 9-10% guidance. Project-wise CAPEX split was not shared. Consolidated unallocable expense of INR 19 crores was mainly a forex loss versus a gain last year.

qa_highlights.question: Sajal Kapoor (Antifragile): How does the group distinguish a temporary setback from a signal to exit, and how does it make decisions in semiconductors and defence without operating history?
qa_highlights.answer: Awuko and Foskor were exited after management gave enough time; it waits at least four to eight quarters before deciding if a trend is temporary. For semicon, it is entering as a supplier of ceramics to fab equipment makers, building on 40-50 years of ceramics experience and working via anchor customers.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya (Kotak): How large are exports in standalone Electrominerals, and is European duty on Chinese imports a driver; what is the semicon 6N and substrate roadmap and any inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Export share has risen from about 20% earlier to 35% last year and is now on a path to 40%. Europe's duties are helping, with US and Asia efforts under way. 5N to 6N powder purity is being worked on; substrate benefits start FY28. Management said the focus is to remain a raw material supplier, with no inorganic plans stated.

risks_watch: Abrasives margin recovery: standalone Abrasives margin fell to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY; oil-linked resin and fuel cost push (about INR 16 crores) and whether normal price increases can offset it, given no further pricing is planned until the cost environment clears.
Awuko winding-up completion (guided within about a quarter) and the exceptional costs still to come; Q1 Abrasives losses from Awuko depress consolidated margins.
Foskor divestment or exit: options being explored, targeted to close by Q2; Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed about INR 17 crores of Foskor loss.

Consolidated Ceramics margin: management expects the high end of 20.5-21% guidance, but standalone Ceramics PBIT was flat YoY on fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.
Sustainability of Electrominerals export-led growth (33% standalone YoY) given that pricing was flat and the growth was mostly volume and mix.
VAW Russia: RUB sales down 14.1% YoY with geopolitical uncertainty; management says it is too difficult to predict and the aim is to stay put.
Unallocable costs: consolidated INR 19 crores in Q1 due to forex loss and lower interest income; forex swings may recur.
key_quotes: Growth at standalone level was broad-based and driven by all three segments.
So, it's going to be very tough and it's going to be tough for us to say that based on which we will start putting up price, etc., is also going to be tough.
We always wait at least four to eight quarters to see whether these are temporary trends or fundamentally things are changing.
Right now our focus is that we should be a raw material supplier and so we stay focused on that.

513375|2026-09.headline: Carborundum Q2 FY27 standalone sales rose 28% YoY to INR 911 crores, a record, while consolidated PAT fell to INR 12 crores on INR 80.3 crores of exceptional items.
513375|2026-09.overview: Standalone sales hit a record INR 911 crores (+28% YoY, +7.7% QoQ), with all three segments growing double digits in H1. Consolidated sales rose 13.1% YoY to INR 1,455 crores, but consolidated PAT after NCI fell to INR 12 crores from INR 75 crores, driven by INR 80.3 crores of exceptional items linked to AWUKO closure and Foskor Zirconia. Management raised FY27 Ceramics guidance to 25-28% growth and margin to 22.5-23.5%, but cut Abrasives margin guidance to 8-8.5% excluding AWUKO. Operating cash flow was weak in H1 on working capital build, which management expects to reverse in H2.

Hosur thin wheel facility established to absorb the Uttarakhand thin wheel operations; qualification under way with 6-7 major international customers.

demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was mainly volume-driven, with a small price contribution; demand supported by industrial, construction and infrastructure activity.

Ceramics exports are about 85%+ of sales; growth led by Engineered Ceramics (including Bloom-related products) and Metallized Cylinders, while wear ceramics also grew.

qa_highlights.question: Where is Ceramics growth coming from, and is export growth driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineered Ceramics (including Bloom-related products) and Metallized Cylinders are the two growth drivers; bare ceramics grew less. Exports are typically 85%+ of Ceramics sales and that ratio held.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AWUKO/Foskor exceptional items arise and are more write-offs expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further AWUKO write-offs are expected; the Foskor exit is on a realisable basis and no extraordinary write-offs are seen, though options are being explored. RHODIUS does not need a write-off.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for standalone Abrasives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views margins as bottomed out at about 10%, with a normal trajectory of 15% to 16%, and is working on pass-through of resin and oil cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow weak and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on strong September sales collected in October-November, and inventory was built for H2 growth. Management expects both to reverse in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue potential exists in semiconductor components and electronic substrates?
qa_highlights.answer: Semiconductor components segment top line of INR 300-350 crores around FY30-31. Electronics substrate timelines are still uncertain; management said at least a year to complete base work and would share later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for RHODIUS?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven targeted by Q1 FY28, followed by small profits. Sales expected flat in FY27 and the loss lower than FY26, after a warehouse move that disrupted the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of VAW Russia volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Status quo: operations remain under the same constraints, with no volume improvement expected in H2.

513472|2026-03.headline: Simplex Castings FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 18% to Rs 202 crore and PAT 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore; FY27 target Rs 300 crore.
513472|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue up about 18% to Rs 202 crore, EBITDA up 20% to Rs 37.39 crore with margin expansion, and PAT up 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore. Q4 revenue was slightly below the prior-year Q4 (about Rs 67 crore cited by an analyst), which management attributed to customer site delays and LPG/gas supply disruptions that held back dispatches. The company received RDSO approval to restart wagon bogie manufacturing, with cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month now built. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs 300 crore and a FY28 aspiration of Rs 500 crore, contingent on execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders.

segments.name: Railways (cast and fabricated bogies)
segments.commentary: RDSO approval received to restart wagon bogies; 200-250 cast bogies a month capacity built. Cast bogie sale value about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Developmental order for fabricated loco bogies; FY27 target Rs 50 crore from cast railway business.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Management targets about Rs 50 crore from power in FY27, linked to BHEL and L&T orders for 32 and 16 coal-based thermal plants to be commissioned by 2032.

segments.name: Steel (coke oven doors and castings)
segments.commentary: Coke oven door segment estimated at Rs 50-60 crore of about Rs 200-220 crore revenue; management claims about 70% share of India's coke oven doors and expects growth toward Rs 100 crore over 2-3 years. Recent orders from SMS and Thyssen for SAIL stamp-charging batteries.

segments.name: Defence and shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Supplies A-brackets, B-brackets and stern boss castings to shipyards and components to Gun Carriage Factory Jabalpur (Dhanush). Management says margins above 10% but segment, with other rest-of-business, expected at only 15-20% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target Rs 300 crore: about Rs 200 crore from existing business (stated as already closed), Rs 50 crore from cast railway business and about Rs 50 crore from power.
FY27 margins guided similar to FY26; cost-reduction gains expected to show in Q3-Q4 FY27.
EBITDA/PAT margin floor of 8-10% reiterated as minimum goal.
FY28 revenue aspiration of about Rs 500 crore, dependent on execution, acquisition and EPC, and railway orders.
FY27 capex planned at Rs 25 crore.

Second preferential issue of about Rs 50 crore; about half earmarked for fabricated bogie facilities (Rs 25 crore capital and Rs 25 crore working capital).
FY27 capex target Rs 25 crore; FY26 capex about Rs 15 crore.
Spare land available at both Bhilai and Rajnandgaon units for expansion and semi-mechanisation.
Centrifugal rolls project (Rs 1.5-2 crore investment) dropped after market survey.
demand_pricing: Wagon bogies: wagon makers about 70-75% of market and railways spares about 20-25%; management targets both channels.
Possible wagon mega-order: management estimates 6,000 bogies (about 2 tonnes cast weight each) for 8,000-10,000 wagons over 3 years, with 20-30% typically outsourced.

Coke oven doors: India has an estimated 150-180 batteries; replacement demand about 3-4% a year; order flow of 2-3 batteries a year, plus about 70-80 batteries for planned 140 million tonne capacity expansion by 2030-2040.
Power and steel demand strong; management says it has become choosy on orders.
Gas (LPG) supply disruptions hit fabrication plants and top line in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue fall YoY versus last Q4 (about Rs 67 crore), and what drove margins higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dispatches slipped because customer site activity was delayed, leaving finished goods inventory that was expected to be realised in April-May. Gas (LPG) shortages also hit fabrication plants. Management said the margin goal is at least 8-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company supply full bogies or only parts, and what is the realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The company assembles bogies from its own castings plus outsourced springs, side bearers, brakes and pads. Cast bogie sale value is about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Couplers and draft gears are planned later.

qa_highlights.question: When will orders from RDSO approval arrive and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: An order of 100-200 bogies is expected in about a month. No further capex is needed for the cast bogie line; it is awaiting the prototype and first order.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 targets, margins, acquisitions and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue target is Rs 300 crore, with margins similar to FY26. Two acquisition talks remain open after one failed; they are in the same line of business. FY27 capex is Rs 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coke oven door market size and share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates 150-180 batteries in India, 3-4% annual replacement, and about 70% market share. Coke oven doors are about Rs 50-60 crore of revenue, with growth to about Rs 100 crore expected over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 Rs 500 crore target risk and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Risks are execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders. qa_highlights.question: How does the Vriddhi Council work and will the ₹50 crore savings be realised in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Council is a group of project leaders running cost and productivity initiatives (material, power, manpower, pricing, VAVE, dies and tools), meeting monthly under a steering committee chaired by the MD. 513509|2026-09.headline: Kalyani Forge Q2 FY27 revenue fell about 18% QoQ to Rs 54.4 crore on plant shifts, but EBITDA margin held at 14.2%, a fourth straight quarter above 14%.
513509|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 54.4 crore, down about 18% QoQ, as a 2,500-ton press was reconditioned and the driveline machining plant was moved from MCD3 to MCD1 over two months. Receivables rose to about Rs 141 crore because of a bank changeover that delayed customer remittances and slower lifting by legacy customers. The board approved a Rs 45 crore funding plan (equity about Rs 10 crore, debt Rs 20 crore, asset and inventory monetisation up to Rs 20 crore).

513519|2026-03.headline: Pitti Engineering FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR1,953 crore and adjusted EBITDA 20% to INR326 crore, with a new INR290 crore casting capex announced.

513519|2026-06.headline: Pitti Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹529 crores, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 16.8% and Lamination FY27 volume target raised to 82,000 tons.
513519|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 16% YoY to ₹529 crores and adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to ₹89 crores, with margin at 16.8%. Adjusted PAT was ₹32 crores versus ₹26 crores a year earlier. Lamination and assembly volume grew 19% to about 19,200 tons, and management raised its FY27 Lamination target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons. Management said the ₹150 crore capex (sheet metal capacity now 108,000 tons) has just commenced, while the ₹290 crore Hyderabad greenfield casting project is about ₹60 crores spent. Margins were flat YoY, which management attributed to pre-operating manpower and variable costs ahead of operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Which applications drive high value Stator and Rotor assembly growth (~37% volume vs 16% for Lamination), and what is EBITDA per ton for integrated assemblies?

qa_highlights.question: Is the export flatness a timing issue or customer delays, and are there new Data Center export customers?

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat despite better product mix?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ₹290 crore Hyderabad casting capex roadmap and Bangalore plan?

Bangalore facility (not board-approved) would be ~₹200 crores building plus ~₹200 crores equipment, in FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY28-FY29 volume and capacity plans, and when is the next capacity capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Sheet metal headroom is only ~8,000 tons at 80% efficiency on 108,000 tons capacity. FY28 capacity capex is expected around Q3-Q4 FY27. Management sees ~17-18% volume growth over three years but cautioned that Mining, Oil & Gas and Data Center demand can shift quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and why has interest cost not fallen?

qa_highlights.question: How will the state capex incentive (other income) run in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The earlier ₹220 crore capex incentive is exhausted. The ₹400 crore expansion would yield ~₹40 crores a year, but the eligibility certificate covers a 7-year period. Management expects no incentive income this year, and about ₹70 crores receivable in 9-12 months; a 9-year period, if approved, could change timing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and PAT targets apply for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA is roughly ₹370 crores on current outlook. FY28 at 90,000 tons: turnover about ₹2,500 crores and EBITDA margin 17-17.2%, excluding incremental Lamination capex. No PAT target was given.

513519|2026-09.headline: Pitti Engineering Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.3% to INR581 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.8% on forex, fuel/power and raw material costs.
513519|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR581 crore (up 16.3% YoY) and H1 revenue about INR1,110 crore (up roughly 15%), with results now reported standalone after merging two subsidiaries in September 2026. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to INR91 crore, but margin was 15.8%, hit by a INR4.61 crore forex loss, higher consumables/packing, fuel and power costs, and higher employee costs ahead of new capacity. Adjusted PAT fell to INR36 crore from INR43 crore, as Q2 FY26 included INR21 crore of Maharashtra incentive income that is now deferred to next year. Management announced a new INR450 crore lamination and machining capex (to FY31) on top of the INR290 crore Hyderabad project, and reiterated FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Q2 forex loss was INR4.61 crore, booked in other expenses above EBITDA. Q1 FY27 figure not available on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover to 16-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel and power costs to be passed on from January and expected to normalise by Q4; steel is a quarterly pass-through. Inflation depresses percentage margin even when passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trade payables increase sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Why defer the Maharashtra incentive?

514043|2026-03.headline: Himatsingka Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose about 5.8% to INR721 crores, with management pivoting into yarn, fabric and apparel adjacencies.
514043|2026-03.overview: Consolidated total income was INR721 crores against INR681 crores a year earlier, up about 5.8%. Q4 other income of about INR100 crores was mostly foreign exchange gains of roughly INR95 crores from rupee depreciation. Utilisation was 99% in spinning, 56% in sheeting and 63% in Terry Towel, with delayed outbound shipments to some jurisdictions and Middle East impacts expected to persist into Q1 FY27. Management framed FY26 as volatile due to US tariffs and the Middle East war, and announced a shift toward yarn, fabric and apparel solutions using existing infrastructure.

514043|2026-06.headline: Himatsingka Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell to INR634 crores from INR661 crores, with EBITDA of INR101 crores (~16% margin).
514043|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income was INR634 crores against INR661 crores, described as range-bound, with shipment deferrals linked to Middle East geopolitical issues and lower capacity utilisation in some divisions. EBITDA came in at INR101 crores, a margin of about 16%, attributed to lower revenue, product mix tweaks and raw material inflation. Management said the call was mainly about the strategic transition to a multi-vertical model using existing assets: Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions have started and are ramping up, Apparel Solutions is due a couple of quarters out, and Home Textiles (especially Sheeting) will be rightsized. Net leverage was described as range-bound at about INR2,550 crores.

segments.name: Yarn Solutions
segments.commentary: Spinning assets (211,584 spindles, described as world's largest single-roof plant) being converted from captive to independent business; over 90% of capacity to be sold externally. Full-capacity revenue potential about INR1,000 crores.

segments.commentary: Uses shared sheeting and knit processing capacity of about 90 million meters by year-end (vs 61 million meters earlier for home textiles, excluding knit). Full-capacity revenue potential about INR1,000 crores; revenue generation has started.

segments.commentary: Planned for Phase 2, expected to launch a couple of quarters later; no revenue contribution discussed yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the positives and negatives this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Negatives were revenue and offtake overhangs; positive is the start of the transition to the new multi-vertical model, which needs no expansion or capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise so much debt and how do tariffs affect the US business?
qa_highlights.answer: The recent NCD raise balances debt tenors and maturities and is not incremental capital. US tariff policy flip-flops created inflation and altered demand; tariff outlook has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: How will fabric capacity of 90 million meters be used versus the 61 million meters home capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The 61 million meters excluded knit platforms; combined 90 million meters will be allocated between Home Textile Sheeting and Fabric Solutions from common infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: How much yarn capacity will be sold externally and is more capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 90% of yarn capacity to be sold externally; capex kept to maintenance and organic needs only.

qa_highlights.question: Will lost Home Textile revenue be replaced in the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for range-bound revenue, but Sheeting will be rightsized; Yarn and Fabric each target about INR1,000 crores at full capacity (about INR2,000 crores combined), with no quarterly split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Sheeting ramp-down about profitability or US challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: US market share loss, tariff-driven pricing pressure and client concentration led to repositioning the business as Himatsingka 2.0.

514183|2026-03.headline: Black Rose Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% and EBITDA about 90% YoY, with EBITDA margin up to 11% from 9.7%, helped by stock-and-sale model and price normalisation.
514183|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 showed a sharp jump, with revenue up 38% and EBITDA up about 90%, driven by the stock-and-sale model in distribution and growth in manufacturing. For the full year, standalone revenue dipped slightly as chemical prices corrected from the start of the year through March 2026, while volumes grew in domestic distribution and acrylamide liquid and NMA. The company stayed debt-free, inventories fell, and a 125% dividend was recommended. Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA or revenue numbers, saying only that top line is targeted to grow over FY26 at current prices.

financial_highlights.change: up from 9.7% in the prior year

financial_highlights.value: about 35% of prior-year revenue; balance from distribution

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 EBITDA run-rate referenced in Q&A
financial_highlights.value: about Rs 13 crore per quarter (as cited by analyst; not disputed)

segments.name: Chemical distribution
segments.commentary: Backbone of the company; stock-and-sale model ensured uninterrupted supply through the Middle East disruption and supported Q4 revenue and margins. Merchant exports fell due to US tariffs and weaker US oil and gas offtake, though a strong export order pipeline is expected to convert in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Acrylamide liquid
segments.commentary: Capacity 32,000 MTPA, of which 20,000 MTPA is for merchant sales and the balance is captive. Volumes grew on new domestic and export customers after exiting the Morbi ceramic binder business; margins improved on raw material management. Export demand picked up in the second half of the current quarter.

segments.name: Acrylamide solid
segments.commentary: Capacity 3,600 MTPA. Volumes stable despite continued imports from China; management calls the business steady.

segments.name: N-methylol acrylamide (NMA)
segments.commentary: Capacity 2,000 MTPA. Significant volume growth in FY26; company is the sole supplier to a key Indian customer. Volumes guided stable for the coming period, with new customer additions as the focus.

segments.name: Polyacrylamide (PAM) solid
segments.commentary: In R&D and piloting; commercialisation targeted within FY27. Specialty amines project with Koei Chemicals is progressing, with an investment decision expected in the current year.

Management said chemical prices had normalised after a long period of subdued levels and expects them to stay normal for some time.

qa_highlights.answer: Margins depend on market conditions and are hard to predict long term. Absolute EBITDA should be sustainable; margin percentage is price-driven, and prices have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q4 EBITDA of about Rs 13 crore per quarter be maintained, and was it inventory gain or operating income? (Madhur Rathi)
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was a mix of inventory gain and operating gain, with volumes rising. Only a 15-day period was affected by the war. No quarterly figure was confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of permanent revocation of the plant closure directions? (Vishwendra Singh)
qa_highlights.answer: The closure notice has been permanently revoked, so operations continue without interruption.

qa_highlights.question: Effect of new products on the top line? (Shweta Agarwal)
qa_highlights.answer: New products are being added in both distribution and manufacturing. The target is higher top line than FY26 at current prices, depending on market penetration and prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Rs 50 crore EBITDA be achieved in FY27? (Madhur Rathi)
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, saying too many factors drive it.
