qa_highlights.answer: No numbers given. Management said revocation and capacity expansion are unrelated, and the aim is maximum utilisation plus pipeline products.

514211|2026-06.headline: Sumeet Industries Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 3.24% (EBITDA INR8.85 crore) on raw material volatility, while management guides ~6% margin and 30%+ revenue growth for FY27.
514211|2026-06.overview: Revenue (income) rose over 9% YoY to INR272.74 crore, but EBITDA was INR8.85 crore (3.24% margin) and PAT was INR1.14 crore, which management attributed to crude-driven PTA/MEG volatility, higher freight costs and a 15-day maintenance shutdown. Production fell 17% QoQ, with sales supported by inventory liquidation. Management said the rights issue (INR199.75 crore gross, net ~INR194.90 crore) is being deployed to working capital, the Nakoda CP plant, debt repayment (~INR23 crore) and a 6.5 MW solar plant. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 30%+ revenue growth, ~6% EBITDA margin and 3.5–4% PAT margin, with the Nakoda plant now guided for Q2 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~20%+ in prior three-four quarters per analyst

segments.name: POY / FDY / texturised yarn (value chain)
segments.commentary: Management said value-added yarn is now 30–35% of yarn production. Demand described as good across POY, FDY and texturised yarn, with no demand issue if the Middle East conflict settles.

segments.name: PET chips (CP plant)
segments.commentary: Existing CP capacity cited as 300 tpd, with yarn drawing at 240 tpd. The acquired Nakoda CP plant (140,000 tpa) is expected to roughly double total capacity once commissioned.

FY27 EBITDA margin of around 6%, expected by end of FY27.

Power cost benefit of around INR25 crore per annum once renewable power is fully commissioned; remaining solar capacity expected in Q4 FY27.
Finance cost expected to fall significantly as debt is repaid and CC interest is reduced.
capex_capacity: Nakoda CP plant (acquired from Narkoda Ltd under CIRP for INR23.47 crore): 140,000 tpa PET chips capacity; new machinery ordered and restoration underway; commissioning guided for Q2 FY28.
Recent 30 tpd (about 20,000 tpa per analyst's reference) capacity addition: partly commissioned in July, remainder in August 2026; management said it is at optimum within about a month.

Rights issue: 16.84 crore shares at INR11.86, raising INR199.75 crore; net ~INR194.90 crore allocated ~INR100 crore working capital, ~INR50 crore Nakoda operationalisation, ~INR23 crore debt repayment, ~INR22 crore solar captive plant.
Captive solar: 6.5 MW captive solar plant referenced; renewable share of power currently ~30%, rising to 25–30% more after new solar commissions (management wording was inconsistent on the share).
Total capex envelope of ~INR90 crore cited by an analyst; management confirmed the Nakoda INR23 crore payment is included in it.
demand_pricing: Management said end-market demand from apparel, home textiles and industrial applications remained healthy; the margin squeeze was input-cost driven.
Raw material (PTA/MEG) prices have declined from peaks but not back to pre-war levels; management expects normalisation by end of August 2026.
Pass-through lags: order cycle ~15 days; management said prices that moved up and down within 15 days could not be fully passed to customers.
Customer base is largely agents; management said the top 10 agents account for approximately 50% of revenue (analyst later noted 41%).
Export: no exports to date; deemed exports under way and direct exports planned, with no special certification needed.
Receivables: management said no receivable is older than 6 months; collection 30–45 days; supplier credit about 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: Volumes delivered in Q1 between POY and FDY?
qa_highlights.answer: Production fell 17% QoQ due to raw material scarcity and a 15-day maintenance shutdown; sales were maintained by liquidating existing stock. No split by POY and FDY was given.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt post-repayment and finance cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited long-term debt of INR86 crore and short-term borrowings of INR74 crore (pre-repayment). After ~INR23 crore repayment, remaining machine term loan expected around INR30 crore; finance cost expected to fall significantly, with CC interest near negligible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin 3.24% vs the ~6% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to volatile raw material prices, weekly swings and pass-through lags; it said the 30,000 tpa addition, renewable power in H2 and falling raw material costs should help margins recover.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin path from ~15% to 25%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects gross margins above 25% and sustained, citing normalised operations and falling raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: Nakoda plant timing and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is guided for Q2 FY28 (first quarter of next financial year cited as Q2); optimum utilisation within about 60 days of commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Tax losses and investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no tax credit remains as past losses were fully utilised. Of INR15 crore investments/loans, INR9 crore is in High Urja, a power company.

qa_highlights.question: Stock price weakness after rights issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on share price, saying selling pressure was expected after the rights issue at INR11.86 versus trading near INR34–35, and expressed confidence in results.

risks_watch: Execution risk on Nakoda CP plant: commissioning timeline (Q2 FY28) and 60-day ramp-up are management estimates.

Guidance credibility: a 3.24% Q1 EBITDA margin vs a ~6% full-year target requires a sharp H2 step-up.

Working capital usage: INR100 crore allocated while bank limits were said to be fully utilised.

514234|2026-03.headline: Sangam India FY26 revenue crossed INR3,200 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR83 crore; Q4 PAT INR33 crore on INR880 crore revenue.

Q4 FY26 revenue was INR880 crore, EBITDA INR98 crore and PAT INR33 crore. Management attributed profit growth to high capacity utilisation and operational efficiency, and denied any one-time inventory gain in Q4 despite the West Asia war lifting crude-linked input prices. Management is preparing a new capex cycle but has not finalised it; renewable power and captive fibre are the stated priorities.

514234|2026-09.headline: Sangam India Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for first time at INR1,045 crore (+33% YoY), with PAT of INR53 crore, a record.
514234|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the best quarter in Sangam's history, with revenue of INR1,045 crore (+33% YoY), EBITDA of INR127 crore and PAT of INR53 crore, all record highs. H1 revenue was INR1,906 crore and H1 PAT INR94 crore, already above full-year FY26 PAT. Management reiterated the aspiration to at least double FY26 PAT in FY27, while debtor days rose to 77 from 67 in March and net debt to equity rose to 1.15x amid a INR1,500 crore capex programme. Operating cash flow was negative in the quarter, and management guided it positive by March 2027.

514448|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% YoY to a record quarter on ~16% volume growth; EBITDA margin held near 27% before VAM-driven price hikes.
514448|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 18% YoY on nearly 16% volume growth, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with EBITDA margin steady at about 27%. FY26 volume growth was about 8% against 11% in FY25. Raw material VAM prices roughly doubled (management cited INR 80-75 earlier versus INR 160-180 now), and the company has passed through about 60-70% of the increase via price hikes effective early April and 1 May, with a further hike from around 15 May. Management declined to give explicit FY27 guidance, but said it aims for 15-20% volume growth to reach INR 500 crore revenue in two to three years. Receivable days rose to about 150-160 days, which management attributes to new-state dealer build-out and expects to normalise over two to three quarters.

514448|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY (about 10% volume, 7% price) while EBITDA margin fell to about 14.4% on raw material spike.
514448|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY in Q1 FY27, with roughly 10% from volumes and about 7% from price increases taken in April and mid-May. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.4%, which management attributed to 6-7 percentage points of raw material cost inflation (VAM spike linked to West Asia tensions) plus about 3-4 points of aggressive dealer-meet and sales promotion spend. Management guided back to a 22-25% EBITDA range longer term and said it is too early to commit to 28-29% in Q2. Working capital weakened, with receivables around INR 145-150 crore (debtor days above 150) and inventory higher, and management targets 120 days over the next two to three quarters.

517041|2026-03.headline: Ador Welding Q4 FY26: revenue up ~3% YoY, EBITDA ~INR38 crore (+200 bps), with management guiding to 100–200 bps further EBITDA margin gains.
517041|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 revenue growth of about 3% YoY, EBITDA of about INR38 crore (up 200 bps) and gross margin of about 36%, excluding the Kuwait recovery and exceptional items. For FY26, standalone revenue grew about 2%, gross margin rose about 250 bps to 38%, and the Kuwait recovery of INR14 crore lifted PBT to about INR130 crore excluding the Uran onerous cost. The Flares and Process Equipment division has been folded into a single welding segment, with loss-making large projects being wound down in favour of product-line business. Management declined to give formal guidance, but flagged Middle East dispatch disruption in March, a Saudi market that is now the third-largest export market, and a longer-term aspiration to triple earnings.

financial_highlights.change: recovery of 2020-21 receivables, booked as impairment reversal

segments.name: Welding (consumables, equipment, MNR)
segments.commentary: Now the only reported segment after the Flares and Process Equipment division was merged in. Management says welding is growing roughly in line with steel consumption and that domestic India is about 80%+ of sales. Consumables and equipment are said to grow in similar cycles, with equipment spiking during capex upcycles.

segments.commentary: Folded into the welding business effective around end-March 2026 and run as product lines of INR20-30 crore. Management says there is no further loss, and that the Uran project is about 96-97% complete. The Q4 result included a INR3 crore gain from an ONGC reorder.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance, but expects EBITDA margin to improve by a further 100-200 bps over coming periods, partly via gross margin, and sees it as feasible within FY27 barring severe supply shocks.
Aspirational target: revenue of INR2,000 crore by FY29 (roughly 25% CAGR) is still referenced, but management says the main principle is to triple earnings over the period.
Management's planning assumption is growth at least in line with IIP/GDP (6-8%), and it believes it can outperform that.
Capex is guided at about INR30-35 crore for FY27 (maintenance INR10-12 crore; two to three new consumable lines), possibly up to INR40 crore a year over the next two years.

Management says it would be feasible to reach INR1,500-1,600 crore of welding revenue by FY28 only if the economy stays strong, which implies about 18-20% growth a year; it has not committed to that figure.
Exports were flattish in FY26 (last year's total cited as about INR154 crore), with a better outlook from order book and approvals.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation is about 70% on a fair estimate, with some lines running at 90-95% and needing capex.
Normal sustainable operating range is cited as 70-90% depending on equipment age and technology.
Two to three new consumable lines are due this year and next, all in welding consumables rather than equipment.
Capex needed to double volume over five to seven years is estimated at INR100-150 crore (plant and machinery, excluding land).
demand_pricing: Demand is described as okay since November-December 2025, but customers are cautious because of inflation in steel and macro conditions.
Around 80-85% of sales go through distributors, so the order book is short-cycle and not a long backlog.

Middle East: March quarter dispatches were hit in the first three to four weeks by the situation there. Most of the pent-up volume was cleared by the end of the quarter, and management says demand remains good.
Saudi Arabia is now the third-largest export market (it was second last year), and inquiries from there have been healthier since December 2025.
Market share is put at about 17-18%, plus or minus a few percent.
Shipbuilding: management says it has approvals for about 75-80% of the required work, but it has not disclosed the revenue from that sector.
Management says it is seeing its best-ever welding automation order book, though the base is still small.
Steel: pricing and inflation are challenging, but management says the cycle is on a brighter footing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are process equipment losses continuing after one-off adjustments, and where does that finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no further negative. The INR3 crore Q4 gain came from an ONGC reorder, the FY26 hit was about INR25 crore, and the division has been restructured into product lines of INR20-30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% EBITDA margin sustainable, and what is the medium-term growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management treats ~12% as the base and aims for incremental, step-by-step improvement. It declined to share internal targets and gave no guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to INR1,500-1,600 crore of welding revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: That would need about 18-20% YoY growth for two years. Management says it is feasible if the economy stays strong, but it would not commit to a number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and were dispatches affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure is high for exports, but management says receivables are secure and demand is firm. March dispatches were hit in the first three to four weeks, and most of the backlog has since cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR30-35 crore, with INR10-12 crore of maintenance. Two to three new consumable lines are coming, with the spend all in welding consumables.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company open to acquisitions, and what is the cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to acquisitions that are more targeted, focused on technology as well as market share. It has not announced any transaction and says the company has a healthy cash balance.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption to dispatches and supply, despite stated strong demand and secure distributor terms.
Steel and supply-chain inflation, which is making customers cautious on orders.
Uran project still at about 96-97% completion with commissioning delays, and a possible further ONGC recovery or LD impact.
Pending Indian income tax demand of about INR14 crore, under appeal; BIS magistrate court proceedings listed for June-July 2026.
Management's growth aspirations (INR2,000 crore by FY29; tripling earnings) are not backed by specific guidance.
Export volumes flat in FY26, and the company is reporting only one segment going forward, so less visibility on the breakdown.

517059|2026-03.headline: Salzer Q4 FY26 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, but margins fell to 7% on petrochemical and copper cost pressure; FY27 EBITDA guidance is 9-9.5%.
517059|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income of INR 31 crore (7% margin) and PAT of INR 10 crore. FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR 1,758 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 8% and PAT grew only 3% to INR 54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to plastic (petrochemical-linked) cost increases of 2-3% of margin, copper and silver increases, freight and Middle East disruption. Working capital reached about 30% of revenue against a stated 25% ceiling, and management guided to a return to 25% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance given recent price hikes and April volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance cut to 9-9.5% for FY27 (whole year). A further 7-10% price increase in June 2026 is planned; Q1 pressure expected, with margin stabilising in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the wires and cables EBITDA margin so low, and does the segment cover its interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly B2B (about 70% per the answer), and copper cost rise means a fixed absolute profit is now a lower percentage (margin was 6.5-7% a couple of years ago). Management said the business earns about 2-3% PAT after interest.

qa_highlights.question: Would management consider demerging wires and cables or other shareholder value unlocking steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the suggestion was taken positively and would be looked at, with no commitment or timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital and short-term debt risen, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital reached about 30% of revenue versus a 25% ceiling, due to margin erosion, smart meter capex and slow scale-up. Management expects a return to 25% or below in FY27. Receivable days are 90-95 on net sales basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi plant business model and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant aimed at local content requirements in Saudi projects; delayed about six months; Phase-1 capex about INR 15 crore; target INR 100 crore revenue for GCC.

517059|2026-06.headline: Salzer Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR498 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 6% and management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 8-8.5% from 10%.

EBITDA (excluding other income) fell to INR31 crore from INR42 crore, with margin at 6%, and PAT dropped to INR8 crore from INR17 crore (2% margin). Management attributed the compression to copper, silver and plastic input inflation with a lag in passing costs to customers in switchgear, which is not on a cost-plus model. Management now expects margins to normalise from Q3 with FY27 EBITDA around 8-8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hikes has been accepted, and what is still pending?

qa_highlights.question: Can cost-plus pricing or hedging protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids cost-plus on standard switchgear to avoid opening cost sheets to customers, and does not hedge commodities beyond natural inventory hedging.

qa_highlights.answer: Wire & Cable is about 70% white-labelled on a cost-plus basis, so margins are stable. Switchgear is not cost-plus, and margin fell about 4.5 percentage points over two quarters.

517146|2026-06.headline: Usha Martin Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore and EBITDA grew 44% to INR 208 crore at a 20.1% margin.
517146|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44% to INR 208 crore and margin up 380 bps YoY to 20.1%. Value grew faster than volume, driven by pass-through of input costs, a richer mix of value-added rope and plasticated LRPC, and a higher rope share. Wire rope volumes were marginally down as the Middle East fell about 28%, while India, the US and Europe grew. Operating cash flow was about INR 242 crore (116% of EBITDA), and free cash flow was INR 135 crore after INR 73 crore capex. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-12% rope volume growth and about 15% value growth, with a 20% minimum EBITDA margin base.

Domestic rope volume up about 12% and value up about 21%. Middle East volume fell about 28% while realisations rose about 36%, holding revenue broadly flat.

segments.name: Wire and Strand (Wires)
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 19% and revenue up about 32% YoY; largely domestic, with early European supply in automotive and rockfall protection. Wire realisation about INR 85,000 per ton.

segments.name: LRPC (black and plasticated)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 3.9% YoY despite a volume decline; plasticated LRPC posted its highest volume and value to date. First international plasticated LRPC order for stay cable applications. Blended black and plasticated realisation about INR 79,000 per ton; management flagged some realisation softness from monsoon and project slowdowns.

segments.name: Oceanfibre (synthetic slings)
segments.commentary: Revenue has trended up for five consecutive quarters, now about GBP 2-3 million per year with a GBP 10 million target over the next few years. Gross margin 65-70%; estimated TAM INR 1.5-2 billion.

qa_highlights.question: How much volume loss came from the Middle East, and what is the outlook for rope volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rope volumes were marginally lower, with Middle East down about 28% and Asia Pacific seeing project delays. It reiterated 10-12% volume growth for FY27, conditional on the global situation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and how much did LRPC pricing affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management set a minimum 20% margin base, with quarterly variation in a 20-21% range from product and geographic mix. It said all steel, gas and input cost increases were passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise only about 3% QoQ when steel rose about 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel increase is about INR 7,000 per ton in absolute terms and is recovered in full; it is not a percentage applied to finished-product prices. EBITDA per ton was INR 40,581.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oceanfibre TAM and why are margins high?
qa_highlights.answer: The TAM is estimated at INR 1.5-2 billion and gross margins are 65-70%. The products are specialised heavy-lifting slings for oil, offshore and wind, where steel rope cannot be used, and they need approvals and track record.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plasticated LRPC volume outlook and approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: A major domestic-share customer approval was verbally confirmed with paperwork pending. FY27 target is 3,500-4,000 tons against 2,500 tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.answer: UM Cables is non-core and may be repurposed for value-added wire and rope; management does not want to remain in cables long term. Thailand margins improved and a plan is expected within 6 months, possibly integrating it with India.

So it will be wrong to say that there will not be an impact.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose 13% to INR201.2 crore in FY26 as higher-margin credit, insurance and banking products outgrew AEPS cash withdrawal, credit is expected to turn EBITDA-positive in Q1 FY27, and the Q4 gross margin run rate is INR50-52 crore per quarter versus INR48.6 crore in Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity or capex quantified; growth comes via 16.6 lakh registered agents and 200+ agent points converting to banking outlets, with BC banking-outlet guidelines expected by end-June 2026 and implementation around Q3 FY27, so outlet capacity could scale in H2 FY27 if guidelines land on time.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Customer GTV rose 10.5% to INR127.9 thousand crore, AEPS market share rose to 18.4% from 17.27%, 16.5 lakh accounts opened, and UPI Cash Point runs at about INR100 crore GTV per month targeting about 50% of AEPS volume within 1-2 years.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed and the business is asset-light agent distribution with no utilisation metric reported, so no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides about 20% YoY profitability growth for FY27-FY29 and credit disbursement at about INR20 crore per quarter growing 2x-3x annually, but no formal revenue or margin upgrade was given and merger and RBI timing remain open.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 gross margin fell to INR48.6 crore, INR3 crore below Q3, and H2 revenue trailed H1 on subsidy timing; RBI BC guidelines are still pending and macro stress could hit discretionary spend, though management guided Q4 run rate of INR50-52 crore per quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: already launched (March 2026); further Spice Pay products wi
rows.why: UPI Cash Point launched formally in March 2026 at about INR100 crore GTV per month, the own consumer app with UPI wallet and planned consumer CRM are on the roadmap, and management expects more Spice Pay products within two years.

rows.label: South India expansion via UPI Cash Point and microfinance/gold-loan partners
rows.why: Only about 16% of agents are in South and West versus 84% in North, East and Central, and management set a goal of a North-like presence in South within 2-3 years through partners.

rows.label: Spice Money merger and listing within FY27
rows.when: completion and listing targeted within FY27
rows.why: NCLT first motion is accepted and the shareholder meeting is next, so the merger is on a defined path but timing depends on remaining approvals.

rows.label: Credit interest rate cut from 32-36% toward 24-26%

517214|2026-06.headline: DiGiSPICE Q1 FY27: continuing-business PAT of INR 9 crore; EBITDA INR 8.6 crore; AePS market share dipped to 17.93%.
517214|2026-06.overview: Management framed DiGiSPICE as a holding company whose only continuing business is Spice Money, a banking-agent fintech serving Tier-3 to Tier-5 India. Revenue was flat on a product-mix shift, but gross margin held at INR 48.1 crore as financial product distribution offset seasonal CICO weakness. EBITDA rose to INR 8.6 crore (about 6.5x QoQ) and PAT to INR 6.6 crore from INR 2.8 crore in Q4. The NCLT merger is in its second motion, with completion targeted by March 2027. Management said there are no formal fundraising plans and it is funding growth from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: PAT (continuing business, as stated by Chairman)

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 2.8 crore in previous quarter
up 87% QoQ; up 25% YoY on a like-for-like basis excluding one-time items
BBPS grew 14.2% YoY; share of GTV 15% vs 9% a year ago

segments.name: Payments (AePS / CICO / UPI Cash Point)
segments.commentary: AePS market share fell to 17.93% in Q1 on lower withdrawals in stronger regions, recovering to 18.3% in July; AePS GTV about INR 13,300 crore. UPI Cash Point GTV INR 276 crore; management targets about INR 500 crore exit in Q2. Around 47% of AePS GTV came from agents on subscription packs.

segments.name: Collections (CMS / BBPS)
segments.commentary: Traditional CMS faces commoditisation and price sensitivity; BBPS GTV about INR 1,500 crore, up 14.2% YoY, with share of GTV rising to 15% from 9%. Three new BBPS clients added. Collections are about 10-12% of revenue.

segments.name: Financial product distribution (CASA, credit cards, insurance, lending)
segments.commentary: Management says this is the growth engine: GTV up 16.3% QoQ and margin up 50.7% QoQ. Grahak loan disbursals INR 167.7 crore; 17.8 lakh CASA accounts sold; five new secured card categories; two-wheeler insurance launched in July. Insurance sales moderated in Q1.

segments.name: Credit (own book, Adhikaris and Vyapar MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Disbursed INR 30.8 crore, up 55% QoQ and 2.8x YoY. Breakeven reported in the credit business. Seven lending partners; third-party capital, with first-loss model discussed. No stress reported so far.

guidance_outlook: NCLT merger in second motion; DiGiSPICE to convert into Spice Money as a pure-play listed fintech by March 2027.
Management expects gross margin growth in coming quarters from new products (financial product distribution, UPI Cash Point).
UPI Cash Point exit run-rate of close to INR 500 crore in Q2 FY27 (Rohit Sood).

Discontinued-business structures to be closed by FY27 year-end; discontinued-business costs described as minimal.

capex_capacity: Agent network at 16.85 lakh agents at end Q1, 12.9% CAGR over five years; 13.3 lakh Adhikaris in Tier-4/5/6 towns.

Management said the company is not seeing stress in agent lending or early open-market lending.
Cash-in/cash-out corridor products from the regulator (AePS third-party money transfer) cited as possible tailwind for South and West expansion.

qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Modi said there are no formal fundraising plans; growth is through internal accruals, with capital raising possible later for new engines or customer acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in insurance policy sales, and how will it be accelerated?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Sood said insurance is sold mainly to captive Adhikaris (shopkeeper insurance), which saturated quickly; the company is expanding the product portfolio and changing the distribution construct next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Any early signs of stress in credit repayments or transaction volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Akash Bafna said agent lending shows no stress because agent cash flows are visible; open-market lending is underwritten cautiously on business vintage and model.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AePS market share fall to 17.93%, and can share gains be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Sood attributed the dip to DBT disbursement skew in southern markets where share is lower; share recovered to 18.3% in July.

qa_highlights.question: Can UPI Cash Point reach 50% of AePS, and how is advantage sustained as entry barriers fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 50% a hopeful target and said Q2 exit could be near INR 500 crore; the BC-agent onboarding requirement was cited as a moat for players with large agent networks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected timeline for the merger and listing, and are there residual costs from discontinued businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kapoor said the merger is expected by end of FY27; discontinued-business losses are minimal and reported separately, with structures being closed by year-end.

risks_watch: AePS market share fell to 17.93% in Q1 on DBT disbursement skew toward southern markets; recovery to 18.3% in July needs confirmation in Q2 numbers.

NCLT second motion; merger and conversion into Spice Money targeted by March 2027. Discontinued-business structure closures due by FY27 year-end; residual costs described as minimal but not quantified.

So, as of now, we don't have any formal fundraising plans.
And so far, we have not seen any stress .

Evasive on specifics where asked, e.g. no revenue figure, no insurance numbers, and the 50% UPI Cash Point question was deflected as a "hopeful" target.

517300|2026-06.headline: GIPCL guides FY27 EBITDA to Rs950-1,000 crore at full run-rate, anchored by 600 MW Khavda solar at 33% CUF and Rs355 crore EBITDA.
517300|2026-06.overview: Management held a post-Q4 FY26 conference call (dated 10 July 2026) covering the 600 MW Khavda solar asset, the 500 MW Khavda phase under evacuation constraints, and a planned 750 MW lignite expansion. Solar EBITDA was about Rs332 crore in FY26 and the company guided FY27 EBITDA to roughly Rs950-1,000 crore only once the 500 MW is fully operational. Interest and depreciation are set to roughly double, which compresses PBT in FY27-28. Management also flagged a 200 MW Khavda land-optimisation add and a BESS conversion at the Baroda gas site. Several answers were given as rough estimates and were not reconciled across questions.

Expected FY27 company EBITDA at full run-rate (500 MW commissioned)
financial_highlights.change: Not in FY27 fully; management said it would appear in a full operational year
FY27 guided Rs350-450 crore (figures varied across answers)
Peak debt guided Rs4,500 crore, Rs6,000-6,500 crore including thermal
vs Rs13 crore previous quarter; includes Rs17 crore income tax refund

financial_highlights.metric: Capital work in progress (500 MW Khavda)

segments.name: Thermal (SLPP 1 and 2, lignite)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs1,103 crore; PLF above 75% at SLPP 1 and 80% at SLPP 2 per management. Thermal stations are described as debt-free.

segments.name: Solar - Khavda 600 MW
segments.commentary: Commissioned December 2025 with full CTUIL allocation from November 2025; CUF 33.24% in the current quarter versus about 23% in Q4 FY26 (teething phase). Management expects 30%+ annual CUF.

segments.name: Solar - Khavda 500 MW (phase 2)
segments.commentary: Advanced commissioning in phases of 200 MW, 200 MW and 100 MW, contingent on CTUIL evacuation readiness (post-monsoon, around end-2026). Rs2,065 crore CWIP sits against it.

segments.name: Solar - Raghanesda and other
segments.commentary: CUF about 28-29% at Raghanesda per management. Wind and 75 MW solar contributed Rs86 crore and Rs38 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Khavda solar park (park developer)
segments.commentary: Park allotted 2,375 MW; GIPCL builds 1,100 MW itself and has sold the rest to third parties (Coal India, SJVN, SAEL). Expected net park income Rs20-25 crore a year, O&M revenue Rs50-60 crore, for 25 years.

segments.name: Gas-based stations (Baroda, ~310 MW)
segments.commentary: Idle, with no revival expected given geopolitics. Plan is to convert the site to a 120 MW BESS (GUVNL approved, tender in place), with a further 160 MW planned. Management also said it intends to hive off the gas assets from the books in the next couple of years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line addition of roughly Rs450 crore (Rs400-425 crore from 600 MW Khavda plus Rs30-40 crore from the RE park), per management.
FY27 EBITDA about Rs950-1,000 crore only at full operation of 500 MW; management said this would not appear fully in FY27.
FY27 interest guided Rs250-270 crore and depreciation Rs425-450 crore (rough; will vary with 500 MW commissioning). FY28 guided depreciation Rs550-600 crore and interest Rs400-450 crore.
Dividend commitment reiterated, with PBT dependent on 500 MW commissioning timing; FY27 PBT guided around Rs220 crore.

750 MW lignite expansion: capex about Rs6,000 crore (Rs4,800 crore debt at 80:20, Rs1,200 crore equity), phased from 2027 to 2032-33. Tender with BHEL under evaluation; order expected by end of FY27 or Q4.
BESS: Rs250-300 crore capex for 120 MW at Baroda, around one year to operational, indicative Rs6 per unit cost; 200 MW Khavda add at Rs800-1,000 crore project cost (timing dependent on land).
capex_capacity: 600 MW Khavda solar commissioned December 2025; 500 MW phase 2 in stages (200/200/100 MW), dependent on CTUIL evacuation line, targeted by end-2026.
Khavda PGCIL connectivity expected by end of July 2026 per management; installation possibly from August.
750 MW lignite expansion, approval in principle from GUVNL under Section 62 cost-plus; capex ~Rs6,000 crore phased 2027-2033.
Additional ~200 MW solar at Khavda using optimised land, targeted within a couple of months; 200-300 MW solar addition envisaged over the next couple of years.
Lignite fuel stated as available for 750 MW plus 500 MW for the full PPA life.
Pump storage: company is bidding for government allocation and identifying sites.
demand_pricing: Solar tariff referenced at Rs2.73/unit; PPAs with GUVNL with 25-year tenure; no curtailment on the 600 MW firm allocation.
Management said Gujarat demand exceeds supply and GIPCL is top of merit order, so it is not exposed to backing down; Khavda evacuation constraints are the exception.
PPAs carry benchmark CUFs; penalties apply to GUVNL below the benchmark. Management says tariffs embed a margin over the CUF.
Management said Khavda CUF would be 29-30%+ annually, Raghanesda 28-29%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue, EBITDA and debt profile for the 600 MW Khavda asset?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue about Rs420 crore at 33% CUF, EBITDA Rs350-360 crore. Debt repayment starts after the one-year moratorium ended June 2026, with step-up repayment over the following years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 500 MW Khavda need more debt, and what is peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term borrowing about Rs4,500 crore post 500 MW commissioning; with thermal expansion, peak debt Rs6,000-6,500 crore. Full disbursement pending against contractor milestones.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY26 Q4 other income Rs42 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly insurance claims settled in FY26 plus Rs17 crore income tax refund, plus government grant amortisation and O&M contractor liquidated damages.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking at BESS and pump storage?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: 120 MW BESS at Baroda gas site under GUVNL approval, with 160 MW planned later; pump storage is in the race for government sites.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 750 MW lignite expansion need equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs4,800 crore would be 80:20 debt and Rs1,200 crore equity, funded via internal accruals over five years, promoter infusion, dilution or market raise; no firm plan yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 310 MW gas stations be revived or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Revival depends on gas prices and geopolitics. Management said the gas assets exist in the books but are technically idle, and hive-off is being considered over the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Khavda evacuation (CTUIL) dependency for the 500 MW phase; commissioning timing and teething losses could hit PBT.

Debt rising from ~Rs3,250 crore to ~Rs4,500 crore and then Rs6,000-6,500 crore with thermal; floating 7.8% coupon exposure.
Monsoon-season CUF dip in Q2 FY27 and the two-to-three-month lag in publishing PLF data.
Equity funding for the Rs1,200 crore equity component of the lignite project is undecided.
Gas-based stations idle; hive-off decision and book-value impact pending.

rows.why: Khavda 500 MW commissioning depends on CTUIL evacuation readiness (post-monsoon, around end-2026), and interest/depreciation roughly double (interest Rs107-110 crore currently vs Rs250-270 crore FY27) which compresses PBT; FY27 figures were given inconsistently across answers.

517334|2026-03.headline: Motherson posted record Q4 FY26 revenue up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 42% and margin up 200 bps, and FY27 capex guided at about INR 6,000 Cr.

Normalized PAT rose 66% in Q4, while reported PAT absorbed INR 177 Cr post-tax of European transformation provisions. FY26 revenue crossed INR 1.25 Lakh Cr (+11%), EBITDA margin was 9.5%, and leverage fell to an all-time low of 0.8x. Management flagged copper up about 38% YoY and Middle East-linked crude and polymer inflation, with pass-through recovery expected to lag one or two quarters.

517334|2026-06.headline: Motherson posted record Q1 FY27 revenue, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 26% and margin up 60 bps despite copper, polymer and freight inflation.

EBITDA rose 26% YoY with margin up 60 bps, led by the modules and polymer (MPP) business after European restructuring. Normalized PAT grew 55% YoY, with no one-off items in the quarter. Management flagged copper up 40% YoY, polymer prices in Germany up 55% YoY, and the World Container Index up 40% YoY as headwinds, with pass-through lagging by 1-2 quarters. Cables and wires volume grew 6% YoY, with value up 14%, helped by copper and aluminium inventory gains and an approximately 8% blended price increase. Margins held except at Lloyd, which was hit by lower revenue, and a Rs 283 crore fair-value gain on the Goldi Solar investment was booked in other income. Management declined to give FY27 volume or revenue guidance, citing the uncertain war and inflation backdrop.

517385|2026-03.headline: Symphony FY26 consol revenue fell 28% to ₹1,131 crores; Australia fully impaired, taking PAT to negative ₹141 crores.

Q4 consolidated revenue was ₹338 crores (vs ₹488 crores) and EBITDA margin fell to 15.5% from 21.2%, while gross margin held at 46.4%. Standalone Q4 revenue was ₹199 crores (vs ₹368 crores) on a high base and channel caution, with management pointing to a possible 4 to 6 week summer runway from mid-May.

Management expects Mexico and USA sales to grow significantly in summer 2027 if summer is normal or robust; no numeric target given.

capex_capacity: No further capital allocation to CTPL Australia; management said Australia turnaround to be done without deploying additional capital.

GSK China and Bonaire USA sell through company-owned or retail warehouses in the US; no new capacity commissioning details given.
demand_pricing: India revenue grew 15% despite pre-summer channel inventory overhang; modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large formats) grew over 100%, and modern trade is over one-third of India revenue, with profitability close to general trade.
General trade carried elevated channel inventory from the prior year, which depressed company sales to them; management does not expect 100% modern trade growth to continue.
Standalone exports from India declined due to geopolitical and shipping disruptions; Middle East remains affected and buyer sentiment muted by higher landed costs.
Q1 demand was patchy in North and East India due to uneven weather; no secondary sales expected in the coming quarter, only primary off-season buying.
Coolers in the US are used outdoors and as whole-house or window-mounted units, sold through Home Depot and Lowe's; management said US and Mexico sales were helped by a hot Southwest summer.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales comes from modern trade and e-commerce, and how does its profitability compare with general trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose the exact share for competitive reasons. Modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large formats and regional stores) is over one-third of India top line, with general trade at 60-65%. Modern trade profitability is almost comparable to general trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will input cost inflation such as plastic hit margins in coming quarters, or will it all be passed on given low channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin pressure is expected in the short term because costs remain elevated and depend on how long the war lasts. Symphony will pass on some but not all of the increase; the impact is hard to quantify yet despite value engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the modern trade growth above 100%: share gain, market growth, strategy change, or low base?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the absence of channel inventory in modern trade and e-commerce, versus general trade which carried elevated inventory from the prior year. Management said growth of this scale is unlikely to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What SKUs are driving Bonaire USA growth, and how does its distribution differ from Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: Products are rebranded Indian SKUs, led by the Air Force model, sold to Home Depot and Lowe's, aided by a hot Southwest US summer. Bonaire uses a US warehouse and retailer model, whereas Australia sells mostly to installation companies, with retail still small.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give revenue, EBITDA and PAT for all subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Bonaire USA revenue Rs36 crore (vs Rs27 crore), EBITDA Rs18 crore (vs Rs7 crore), PAT Rs17 crore. IMPCO Mexico revenue Rs54 crore (vs Rs66 crore), EBITDA Rs3 crore (vs Rs7 crore), PAT Rs1 crore. GSK China revenue Rs34 crore (vs Rs24 crore), EBITDA Rs6 crore (vs Rs2 crore), PAT Rs5 crore. CTPL Australia revenue Rs27 crore (vs Rs31 crore), EBITDA negative Rs4 crore, reported PAT Rs36 crore including about Rs42 crore one-time gain that is excluded at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken and what is planned, given raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: No price hike yet in the household cooler segment. Outside household coolers, 7% to 10% hikes have been taken, with more planned in coming days; the extent depends on when the war ends and costs normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy to turn around CTPL Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: No additional capital will be deployed; the impairment and write-off is treated as history from FY26. Management said there is nothing new on product, distribution or manufacturing beyond what is already in place.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BISP product categories beyond exports, and are tabletop fans and water heaters sold online or offline?
qa_highlights.answer: BISP includes large-space ventilated air coolers, tabletop fans (sold year-round), water heaters and exports. Management said these are already in modern retail and GT in top cities, but not yet nationwide. BISP is about 48% of consol revenue and 23% of standalone TTM revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there demand for air coolers in the US, a developed market with high per-capita income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coolers are not seen as a poor man's AC outside India and are sold in the US, Europe and the Middle East. In the US they are used outdoors, as whole-house or window-mounted units in the dry Southwest, and their key advantage is portability and plug-and-play use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Mexico and USA sales, given the summer conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Mexico had two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026), so management expects significant growth in summer 2027 if conditions are normal or robust, without giving a number. USA sales should also rise next summer if the summer is similarly good.

qa_highlights.question: Have export shipments resumed, and are geopolitical issues affecting orders?
qa_highlights.answer: The Middle East remains affected. Higher costs elsewhere have made buyers more cautious, since landed costs rose and they cannot pass on the full increase, so purchases are muted and not yet back to normal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary outlook for the next few quarters, and what are secondary sales trends in July and early August?
qa_highlights.answer: Bonaire USA and GSK China should be fairly good in Q2 FY27 and more muted after that, with Bonaire seeing little revenue in the next two quarters. Q1 was patchy in North and East India. No secondary sales are expected in the coming quarter; only primary off-season buying by channel partners in the current and subsequent quarters.

517385|2026-09.headline: Symphony Q2 FY27 consol revenue rose 31% to ₹275 crore and EBITDA nearly tripled to ₹36 crore, with EBITDA margin at 13% vs 6.4%.
517385|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to ₹275 crore and EBITDA rose to ₹36 crore from ₹13 crore, despite gross margin falling about 4%. Standalone revenue rose to ₹170 crore from ₹155 crore, with standalone EBITDA of ₹30 crore vs ₹27 crore, while standalone gross margin fell about 2.3%. Management said Beyond India Summer Products (BISP) now make up 51% of consolidated top line, with a high-single-digit EBITDA margin. The company announced a second interim dividend of ₹2 per share, taking FY27 interim payouts to ₹3 per share (about ₹21 crore so far), and said it will enter room air conditioners, BLDC ceiling fans and air purifiers on an asset-light, outsourced model.

517498|2026-03.headline: Websol FY26 revenue rose 82% to INR 1,049 crore and PAT 96% to INR 303 crore, with Q4 revenue of INR 401 crore and a INR 1,161 crore order book.
517498|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR 1,049 crore (up ~82%), EBITDA of INR 429 crore (41% margin) and PAT of INR 303 crore (28.6% margin), with Q4 the best quarter on most parameters. The company turned net cash surplus, cash from operations was INR 255 crore, and cell capacity doubled to ~1.2 GW after cell line 2 commissioning in September 2025. Management plans to upgrade one 600 MW Mono PERC line to TOPCon (capacity to 1.35 GW) by February 2027, while Andhra Pradesh expansion timing remains undisclosed beyond a June 2027 target. Margin compression was attributed to a higher module mix, silver costs and softer cell and module realisations.

segments.name: Cells (DCR)
segments.commentary: Combined cell utilisation above 90% in FY26; cell realisation ~13-13.5 cents/Wp, softening with silver cost increases. Cells supplied to module makers and captive use in the company's own module line.

segments.name: Modules (DCR)
segments.commentary: Highest-ever module sales in Q4; module realisation ~22-22.5 cents/Wp. Module line (550 MW, Mono PERC) hit a record monthly utilisation of 80%. Module margins are structurally lower than cell margins and drove most of the EBITDA margin dip.

guidance_outlook: TOPCon upgrade of one 600 MW Mono PERC line to ~750 MW (+150 MW), commercial start targeted February 2027, ~2 months ramp to full utilisation; capex INR 250-270 crore; ~15 days revenue loss for that line.
Management expects to approach full run-rate utilisation across all lines in the coming quarter (Q1 FY27).
Andhra Pradesh expansion (2 GW integrated cell and module phase) targeted for June 2027 per management; details to be announced later, no postponement planned.
Ingot and wafer backward integration, with MOU signed with Linton, targeted to commission ahead of ALMM List-3 deadline of June 2028.
Cell and module margins expected to remain healthy over the next 2-3 years with some variability, per management.
capex_capacity: Cell capacity doubled from 600 MW to ~1.2 GW with cell line 2 commissioned in September 2025, funded entirely from internal accruals.
Mono PERC to TOPCon upgrade takes cell capacity to ~1.35 GW; target cell efficiency above 24.5% (vs ~23.3% for PERC); cell size moving from 182x182 to G12R (182x210).
Integrated 4 GW cell and module plan in phases of 2 GW each; the second 2 GW tranche expected around mid-CY28 on TOPCon, with space reserved for future back-contact upgrade.
Module capacity is 550 MW; cell capacity exceeds module capacity, so about 600-750 MW of cell output is sold to third-party module makers.
Management says there is little scope for further expansion at the existing Falta site.
demand_pricing: Focus is on DCR market, mainly PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar; management reports no demand issues and says its entire line is ALMM-listed and DCR-compliant.
Order book is largely module (60%) and mostly sold through solar pump and module players; the company does not tender directly for government orders.
Current TOPCon DCR cell price ~14 cents/Wp; cell realisation 13-13.5 cents/Wp and module 22-22.5 cents/Wp, described as a softening.
Management says it is seeing more orders than the reported INR 1,161 crore but did not quantify further bookings.
Q4 off-take recovered after Q3 delays that were attributed to temporary customer liquidity stress rather than cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to repay the IREDA loan and release pledged promoter shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt under the IREDA facility is ~INR 92 crore and more than 80% of promoter shares are pledged; advanced discussions are under way, with completion expected in the next month or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 EBITDA margin decline driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop mainly to higher module share in the mix, plus silver cost increases and softer cell sale prices; EBITDA still grew 86% YoY and ~37% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TOPCon upgrade capex, revenue loss and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is INR 250-270 crore for ~150 MW of added capacity; revenue loss is about 15 days for the one line, and ramp-up to full utilisation is ~2 months after February 2027 commercial start.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to lower depreciation lives and what is the FY27 tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon equipment useful life is now 8 years (from 12 years) and Mono PERC is 3 years; all tax credits are used up, so FY27 will be at the standard corporate tax rate.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund the next capex phase?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash covers near-term expansion, with some debt to be raised later; management aims to keep debt levels prudent and said there is no funding concern for now.

qa_highlights.question: Does management see any update on the Andhra Pradesh timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting June 2027, has not postponed the commitment, and will announce details once the funding structure and sequencing are finalised.

517498|2026-06.headline: Websol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 70% YoY to INR373 crore and PAT grew 16% to INR78 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 34% from 47% on module mix.
517498|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR373 crore, up 70% YoY and down about 7% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR126 crore (+21% YoY, margin 34% vs 47%) and PAT of INR78 crore (+16%). Cell output rose to 259 MW (92% utilisation) and module output to 103 MW (81% utilisation), with module volume doubling and driving the margin dilution. The company repaid the INR110 crore IREDA term loan on 4 August from internal accruals, with promoter pledge set to fall from 80% to 16% of promoter holding once released. Phase 3 expansion is being relocated from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, with land approval awaited; management says capex, cost and timelines are unchanged.

Management expects payback of 2 to 3 years on the TOPCon capex; cell efficiency expected around 25% post-upgrade.

Current cell price quoted at about USD0.13 per Wp and module at about INR21 per watt, against Q1 levels of about USD0.125 and INR20.50.

Demand is mainly DCR (PM-Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM); management sees no decline. Inventory rose about 7% QoQ and management attributes it to monsoon-season offtake slowdown and captive cell blocking in modules.
Input costs: silver prices have eased but imported paste carries a lag; wafer prices are flat. The West Asia conflict has raised BOM costs for modules, not cells.
Management said Q1 margin decline reflects lower cell prices and higher silver and BOM cost, alongside mix shift.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited synergies in skilled manpower, supply chain and infrastructure, with no change to capex, project cost, funding or timelines; no financial outflow had occurred on the AP land.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trend and is margin pressure expected to persist?

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects incremental revenue from higher Wp per cell (7.6-7.7 Wp for PERC to about 9.5 Wp for TOPCon), higher capacity (600 MW to 750 MW) and a price premium; it expects a 2-3 year payback on the INR270 crore capex.

517498|2026-09.headline: Websol H1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 734 crore (+89.6% YoY) and Q2 revenue rose 114.6% to INR 361 crore, with EBITDA of INR 128 crore in the quarter.
517498|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the strongest half-year on record, with revenue of INR 734 crore and EBITDA of INR 254 crore in H1. Q2 revenue rose 114.6% YoY to INR 361 crore, EBITDA rose 77.3% to INR 128 crore and net profit rose 73.2% to INR 80 crore. The company repaid its IREDA debt in August and is now debt-free, with cash from operations of INR 244 crore in H1. Management also announced a 4 GW integrated greenfield project at Falta (West Bengal), a TOPCon conversion, and entry into EPC, IPP, solar parks and energy trading.

517506|2026-03.headline: TTK Prestige Q4 FY26 domestic revenue grew 14.4% and company revenue 12.5%, with operating EBITDA of INR81.7 crore, up 43.8%.
517506|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was driven by domestic demand, with induction cooktops giving a short-term boost to appliances, and exports constrained by supply chain disruption. Operating EBITDA rose 43.8% to INR81.7 crore and PBT rose 35.9% to INR71.9 crore, though exceptional charges relating to the new Labour Code were incurred. Gross margin expanded despite commodity inflation, which management attributed mainly to inventory management and mix, with the mid-quarter price hike only partly visible. For FY26, company revenue grew 9.6% (domestic 9.8%), operating EBITDA grew 12% and PAT rose about 14% to INR185 crore. Management flagged input cost inflation of about 10% post the West Asia conflict and expects margins to dip during the ongoing investment phase.

517506|2026-09.headline: TTK Prestige Q2 FY27: total sales up ~21.9% and domestic up ~23.4%, with operating EBITDA up ~70.9%, but management flags inflation pressure reaching gross margin.
517506|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter with robust top-line growth and better profitability, driven by domestic demand, premiumisation and new product launches. Growth was about 22% in total sales, with about 8-9 points from volume and the rest from value/mix. Two exceptional items were booked this quarter: the divestment of the 51% subsidiary Ultrafresh Modular Solutions and a write-off of the CCD investment in a rural distribution startup (INR 2 crore). Management said raw-material and packaging inflation is still rising, that the industry has not fully absorbed it, and that gross margin will start to feel the stress from here. Management declined to give fresh margin guidance, but reiterated a steady-state EBITDA potential of 13-14%.

segments.name: Cookers
segments.commentary: Contributes around 30-32% of sales as stated by management. Triply cookers are growing at about 1.5x the industry average.

segments.name: Cookware
segments.commentary: Contributes around 15-18% of sales. Enamel and ceramic are early-stage categories, with a few enamel SKUs launched and expansion under way.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Contributes close to 50% of sales. Outsourced to exclusive partners. Induction is growing faster than company growth, with management expecting high-teens growth going forward.

segments.name: Horwood (UK subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Top line has grown well, but cost inflation from geopolitical issues and the UK/Europe economy has pushed bottom line close to breakeven. Management expects steady top-line growth.

segments.name: Judge and Prestige brands
segments.commentary: Both brands are growing robustly. Judge is positioned at the lower end of the mass market and carries a structurally lower margin than Prestige. Management said cannibalisation is minimal.

guidance_outlook: Steady-state EBITDA potential remains 13-14%, but management declined to give near-term margin guidance given cost volatility.
Strategic spend outlay of INR 200-250 crore over three years; about INR 100 crore spent over the last six to eight quarters, so roughly INR 150 crore left. Spend will shift to brand and innovation.

Further price increases are needed to pass on prior cost increases, but the timing is undecided. Management said the industry has not fully absorbed costs yet, and cost pressure will continue into the next few quarters.
Some festive-season sales will flow into Q3 FY27; October has been good.
Induction is expected to grow in the high-teens % in a stabilised state, down from earlier triple-digit growth rates.
capex_capacity: Triply circles are imported, with China as a dominant source; there is no domestic production of triply circles.
Around 90% of kitchenware is manufactured in-house; appliances are fully outsourced to exclusive partners.
Inventory days were not higher, but absolute inventory value rose on demand anticipation and manufacturing system improvements. Management said it will slow the build if demand does not justify it.
No capacity or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: Industry demand has revived in the last few quarters, driven by urban premiumisation, kitchen modernisation, and a shift from unorganised to branded players.

Commodity cost inflation affects about 95% of input line items, including stainless steel, aluminium, packaging, handles, rubber and chemicals. Management said current prices are well above Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 levels.
Price increases have been staggered across the industry, with TTK taking a step-up first. Management said the industry has not fully absorbed costs yet.
E-commerce and quick commerce together make up around 20% of sales, and the share has held steady. Growth is described as evenly distributed across channels.
Competition is most intense in cookware, led by digital-first brands. Management says the impact on growth has not been visible so far.
Exports remain a concern because of the war and global uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Which input costs are rising, how are peers pricing, and how much of the strategic expense has been incurred?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 95% of input lines are affected, with a staggered industry price-increase pattern. Strategic spend was about INR 13 crore in H1 FY27, against INR 85-100 crore in FY26 and INR 20 crore before that, with a three-year outlay of INR 200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall, and will strategic spend continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY26 included about INR 18 crore of strategic expense that did not recur, and cost-optimisation benefits are flowing through. Spend will continue for one more year as part of the three-year programme.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 22% growth is volume versus value, and how much price is still to be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8-9% is volume and the rest is value/mix, helped by premiumisation and triply growth. Management said some prior cost increases still need to be passed on, but the timing is undecided.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 13% EBITDA margin target still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained a steady-state potential of 13-14% EBITDA but declined to guide near-term because of cost volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise and what is the outlook for gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days did not rise. Absolute inventory rose on anticipated demand. The CFO said old-cost inventory benefits are used up, so stress will start to show in gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the induction cooktop growth and competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Induction grew faster than the company, and management expects high-teens growth in a stabilised state. Competition is concentrated in cookware from e-commerce-led brands, with no growth impact seen so far.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure as old-cost inventory is used up and raw-material prices stay high. Price increases may not fully offset this and could hit demand.
Further strategic spend of about INR 150 crore over the remaining period, shifting into brand and innovation, which could keep opex elevated.
Working-capital strain from higher absolute inventory, which needs monitoring in Q3.
Export weakness due to war and global uncertainty.
Horwood (UK) near breakeven because of cost inflation in the UK and Europe.
New digital-first entrants in cookware and the reliance on imported triply circles (China).

key_quotes: The concern continues to be on the rising cost, inflationary pressures, and how do we handle that as we move forward.
On a steady state, we do believe that the business potential is around 13%-14% EBITDA. We maintain that stand.
I think from now on, I think the stress will start coming into the gross margin.
The category, which was probably in low teen growths, would probably continue to be in high teen growth in our view in a stabilized state.

517522|2026-03.headline: Rajratan Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin dipped on a ~INR10,000/ton steel price spike it could not pass on; FY26 sales volume up 18% to over 133,000 tons.
517522|2026-03.overview: Management reported record sales tonnage for FY26 of more than 133,000 tons, up 18% YoY, from three locations (India, Thailand, and the newly merged USA subsidiary). Q4 EBITDA margin fell because steel wire rod rose by almost INR10,000/ton from January to March, which could not be passed on, while energy availability and cost also weighed. Management said the price increases have been passed on from April and expects margins to recover to 13-13.5% in Q1 FY27, with a sustained consolidated band of 13.5-14%. FY27 volume growth target is 17-18%, with Chennai capacity doubling to 60,000 tons by Q2 and steel cord (conveyor belt) trials starting in Q2.

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material consumption as % of sales
EBITDA margin impact from unpassed raw material cost

financial_highlights.change: vs ~11.4% in prior quarter and 13.5% in Q2 per analyst

financial_highlights.value: Gain on FX (USD and Thai Baht appreciation)
Low; Thailand BOI effective rate about 13.9%

segments.name: India (Pithampur/Indore and Chennai)
segments.commentary: India exports were just over 9,000 tons in FY26 and are targeted at about 15,000 tons in FY27. Indore/Pithampur and Thailand are running at about 90% utilisation, with Chennai peaking at 85-90% in March.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Volume about 51,000 tons, guided to grow to 55,000-56,000 tons (10-11%) on debottlenecking. Q4 EBITDA margin about 10%. Thai BOI tax exemption applies beyond 36,000 tons of sales.

segments.name: USA (Rajratan USA, merged)
segments.commentary: Now consolidated; USA revenue cited at INR118 crore. Plan to grow North America about 30% in FY27. Around INR30 crore of cost for the second half is booked in the USA entity on FOB supply.

segments.name: Europe and Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Europe to grow about 50% from a low base; Southeast Asia to grow 10-15%. Japan is an early new opportunity.

segments.name: Steel cord / wire rope (conveyor belt)
segments.commentary: 10,000 ton/year plant at Indore, about INR70 crore capex (INR50 crore spent). Expected top line about INR150 crore at peak, reached in about 2 years (FY29). Current EBITDA margin about 20% per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume growth of 17-18%, implying about 155,000 tons of total sales if conditions remain normal; excludes steel cord volumes.
Thailand FY27 volume 55,000-56,000 tons (10-11% growth); the balance of growth to come from India, mainly Chennai.
Consolidated EBITDA margin: management says to assume 13.5-14% sustainable; Q1 FY27 margin expected to return to 13-13.5%.
Chennai capacity to double from 30,000 to 60,000 tons by Q2 FY27, but FY27 sales expected around 34,000-35,000 tons, with gradual ramp-up.
PLI incentive (8% of incremental sales) is not included in projections; approval uncertain pending change in the ladder requested to the ministries.
Working capital requirement expected to stay high or rise; term loan to fall by under INR50 crore in FY27.
capex_capacity: Chennai: capacity to double from 30,000 to 60,000 tons by Q2 FY27 via balancing equipment; about INR25 crore more to be spent this year, with some machines already installed.

Steel cord (conveyor belt) at Indore: new shed built after the old 1989 shed was demolished; machines being installed, trials from Q2 FY27, full capitalisation by Q3 FY27; about INR50 crore spent with about INR25 crore more needed.
Consolidated capital WIP of about INR88 crore (standalone INR69 crore), of which about INR50 crore is steel cord and about INR20-25 crore is Chennai.
No additional capex plans for FY27 beyond Chennai and steel cord, per management.
State capital subsidy from MP government (30% of 2020 investment) received over 7 years, about INR3.5-4 crore a year; similar subsidy expected for steel cord and reduces the investment cost.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is robust in India, Thailand and globally; no GCC customers remain (exports to GCC are zero), and shipping disruption and port congestion at Singapore and Colombo are the main impact.
Tyre-sector market share back to 42-43% in India, from 35-37%; historic peak 43-44%.
Price increases passed on from April; realisation has moved above INR90,000/ton per the analyst's question, which management confirmed. Export pricing is set on global wire rod prices.
Competition: capacity exceeds demand, some global players may not survive, and new entrants must price lower; management says Rajratan's realisation is at the higher end.
Management expects the auto slowdown has not yet hit but expects a possible slowdown in April-May; this is not confirmed in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 13-14% and can they be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 dip was from the Jan-Mar steel spike, now passed on from April; margin expected to return to 13-13.5% in Q1 FY27, and 13.5-14% is the sustainable consolidated band.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: A new consolidated USA subsidiary (Rajratan USA) is now merged; about INR30 crore of FOB shipping and logistics cost for the second half is booked there, not in Thailand. This could rise with export volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Thailand BOI privilege: income tax is exempt beyond 36,000 tons of sales, giving an effective rate of about 13.9% on the privileged company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking a change in the PLI ladder after missing the year 1 and year 2 production targets; without approval, no PLI is assumed. If approved, it is 8% of incremental sales, about INR40-50 crore over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the steel cord/wire rope business and what is its economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel cord for conveyor belts; 10,000 tons/year capacity, about INR150 crore peak revenue at about INR150/kg, reached in about two years (FY29), current EBITDA margin about 20%. Management says it is a pilot and not a big investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand Chennai when margins and pricing are under pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all Chennai customers are profitable, that market share must be defended, and higher output lowers variable cost; it said 13-14% is a decent margin for investment.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Gains from FX: the USD appreciated against the rupee on larger exports, and the Thai Baht strengthened, reflected in the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Thailand and USA combined EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Thailand Q4 EBITDA margin was 10% (corrected from 7.5% on the call). Management said Thailand and USA business had no substantial change and said it would respond separately on the combined figure.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility: wire rod rose about INR10,000/ton in Jan-Mar, and the company could not pass on costs immediately; margin depends on price pass-through.
Working capital and debt: export credit cycles of 45-60 days plus US duty costs push up working capital; management expects borrowing to stay at about 7-7.5% and not reduce.
Chennai ramp-up risk: 60,000 ton capacity, but FY27 sales targeted at only 34,000-35,000 tons; PLI approval unresolved, with two missed production targets.
Competitive pricing: excess global capacity, possible price cuts by competitors, and risk of volume price trade-off.
Shipping and geopolitics: Middle East conflict, port congestion and shipping delays; management flagged that Q1 dispatch shortages were expected to ease by end of April.
Steel cord/wire rope commercialisation: trials from Q2 FY27 and approvals still needed; volumes not in FY27 base case; wire rope contribution of 2,000-3,000 tons expected at most in FY27.

517522|2026-09.headline: Rajratan targets 15–20% volume growth and a 50,000-ton Thai expansion (~INR100 crore capex), while management calls current 12.7–13% EBITDA margins the floor.
517522|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as revenue and earnings growing faster than volumes, driven by higher utilisation in Chennai and Thailand. Consolidated EBITDA was INR45.79 crore in Q2 versus INR41.71 crore in Q1 (about 10% QoQ, 14% YoY as stated on the call), but EBITDA per ton fell about 3% YoY as input costs rose. Management approved a 50,000-ton Thai brownfield expansion (about INR100 crore) and said Chennai will be ramped from about 30,000 to 60,000 tons over time. Steel cord at Pithampur is still in trials, with about INR70 crore of CWIP not yet capitalised.

segments.name: India (Chennai and Pithampur)
segments.commentary: Chennai is at near full utilisation on the first 30,000 tons, with rated capacity now 40,000 tons and a target of 60,000 tons; FY27 Chennai output guided at 37,000 to 38,000 tons. India volume grew about 14% from H1 to H2 per management.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Running at about 100% of capacity (about 15,000 tons per quarter, actual Q2 production about 14,600 tons); volume growth 22% per management. Premium customers are about 30% to 32% of Thai sales, targeted to reach about 40% in the coming year.

segments.name: Steel cord (Pithampur, conveyor belting)
segments.commentary: In trials; samples to customers expected next month; ISO and BIS certification still pending. Management is not including steel cord revenue in H2 projections; about INR70 crore of CWIP not yet capitalised, expected to be capitalised around end of this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated volume growth of 15% to 20% YoY for at least the next 10 to 15 quarters; FY27 consolidated volume about 160,000 tons.

Thai 50,000-ton capacity expected within about one year (FY28 H2 start per analyst reading); management projects utilisation within about two years; capex about INR100 crore, funded by internal accruals plus bank loans below 4%.
Chennai to reach 60,000 tons; no firm board approval for any capacity beyond that. Management expects Chennai expansion within about two years if returns justify it.
Management says Thai EBITDA will improve in the coming quarter; little EBITDA improvement expected in India for the remaining two quarters.
Steel price increases expected to continue until mid-November; price hikes to be passed on to remaining customers from December onward.
capex_capacity: Chennai: 30,000-ton first phase nearly fully utilised; rated capacity now 40,000 tons with machines added modularly; monthly output rising from 3,500 to 4,000 tons, then 4,500 tons; 60,000-ton target. Prior capex about INR270 crore for 30,000 tons plus INR30 to 35 crore to complete to 60,000 tons.

Thailand: 50,000-ton brownfield expansion, about INR100 crore (INR125 crore including about INR20 crore for an adjacent factory purchase); expected to be running in about one year, with H2 FY28 start per analyst reading.

Pithampur steel cord: about 10,000 tons planned, with in-house lines still to be installed; a new shed of about 2.5 lakh sq ft has been built; capitalisation expected at end of the quarter after trials.
Pithampur bead wire capacity 72,000 tons total, of which 60,000 tons bead wire (per analyst citing presentation; management confirmed).
Management expects India capacity to reach about 142,000 tons including steel cord once complete (per management correction).
demand_pricing: Indian tyre market growing 8% to 10%; no production cuts by tyre customers in the last year (per management).

India export volume target about 14,000 to 15,000 tons this year, roughly 40% growth; drivers are China-plus-one demand and Rajratan being the only Indian exporter; US subsidiary exists and a Europe subsidiary is planned.
Thailand price gap between premium and Chinese customers can reach THB10,000 per ton (about INR25,000 to 26,000).
Working capital: Europe about 70 to 80 days (including about 40 days transit), US about 90 days, local Thailand about 40 days.
Tariffs: US Section 232 duty of 50% on Indian and Thai steel products; China faces an additional 12.5%.

Competition: management named Tata Steel as the bigger rival and Bansal Wire as a newer entrant. Management said pricing should improve in one to two quarters, and it chose to hold share rather than chase low-price customers.

qa_highlights.question: Thai capacity expansion timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about one year to build and two years to fill, with capex of about INR100 crore (INR125 crore including the factory purchase), versus about INR300 crore for a greenfield plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA per ton is down while volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said input costs (gas, power, diesel, packing, freight) rose sharply; it kept EBITDA per ton roughly stable and does not expect operating leverage to show in the numbers; it sees current margins as the floor.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume and revenue growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 15% to 20% volume growth YoY for the next 10 to 15 quarters, with consolidated FY27 volume near 160,000 tons; revenue depends on price.

qa_highlights.question: Green bead wire and Thai export advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Thai feedstock is 92% to 95% scrap-based green steel, which India cannot replicate; this won early approvals with European tyre makers ahead of CBAM. Management declined to forecast the margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: Funding for the Thai capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Combination of internal accruals (Thai balance sheet generating cash monthly) and bank loans below 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Price hikes and margin pressure drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Some hikes taken where prices were not finalised; the rest to be passed on at quarter end. Management said steel prices are rising until mid-November; margin pressure is mainly energy, freight and packing rather than steel.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on price increases; management concedes EBITDA per ton is flat to down YoY and plans to keep competing head-on rather than cutting volume.
Steel cord ramp-up is delayed by certifications (ISO, BIS) and trials; about INR70 crore of CWIP and depreciation and interest will start once capitalised.
Thai utilisation: analyst expects a five to six year fill at 12% to 13% growth; management says about two years, which is a credibility gap to track.
Working capital and borrowings are rising with exports (about 70 to 90 days receivables); consolidated borrowings increased, and the analyst asked for the reconciliation.
Consolidated other income fell sharply QoQ (analyst cited INR3.4 crore to INR0.66 crore); management attributed this to consolidation effects but figures were disputed on the call.
Freight and CBAM volatility under DDP contracts; management is absorbing some risk with freight surcharges.

517536|2026-03.headline: FY26 record revenue of INR 550 crore (+10.5% YoY) and EBITDA of INR 71.9 crore, with gross margin at a record 13.2%.

Operating cash flow and net cash rose to INR 127.3 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR 8 per share. 517536|2026-09.headline: Onward Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR170.2 crore (+22.4% YoY), EBITDA margin 15.6%, and FY27 guidance was raised to 15-18% growth.
517536|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached a record INR170.2 crore, up 22.4% YoY and 13.9% QoQ, with constant-currency growth of 17.7% YoY and 13.5% QoQ. EBITDA rose 33.7% YoY to INR26.6 crore at a record 15.6% margin, and PAT grew 41.2% YoY to INR16.8 crore. Margin gains were helped by an INR2.9 crore UK R&D credit relating to FY26, which management booked in Q2 after approval in September. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15-18% and EBITDA margin guidance to 13.8-14.3%, replacing the earlier "double-digit" language. Receivable days stretched to about 80, which management attributed to fast growth and customer approval delays.
