qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is cautious, is hiring local people in the US, and the guidance already reflects the new regulatory environment.

517544|2026-09.headline: Centum Q2 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to INR 312 crore and PAT 77% to INR 23 crore; order book near INR 2,000 crore (+38%).
517544|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 312 crore (+52% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 40 crore (+63%, margin 12.69%, +87 bps) and PAT of INR 23 crore (+77%, margin 7.31%). H1 revenue rose 32% to INR 517 crore, H1 EBITDA rose 25% to INR 63 crore (margin 12.11%) and H1 PAT rose 28% to INR 36 crore. BTS revenue grew 84% in the quarter and EMS grew 41% YoY (about 42% QoQ). Management said the overseas subsidiaries were deconsolidated from Q1 FY27, so the consolidated numbers now reflect standalone. Supply-chain shortages (PCBs, memories, controllers, MLCCs) remain the main near-term constraint on lead times, prices and working capital.

segments.name: BTS (Build to Spec: radar, electronics, space, defence)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +84% YoY; H1 +33% YoY. Order book INR 959 crore, +47% YoY. Wins include a ~INR 30 crore export EW subsystem order for a global OEM (naval ELINT) and a second tactical air navigation systems order of ~INR 51 crore (GRSE customer).

segments.name: EMS (Electronic manufacturing services)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +41% YoY and ~42% QoQ; H1 +32% YoY. Order book grew 30% YoY. Semiconductor equipment deliveries ramping; management sees the segment reaching a USD 45-50 million annual run-rate in about two years, versus an earlier USD 25-30 million estimate.

EBITDA margin target of 12.5-13% at company level for now, aiming to reach and breach 13% next year, then 14-15% in three to four years.
BTS margin range maintained at about 20-22% long term; quarterly BTS margins can swing on program mix.

Order execution over roughly 2 to 2.5 years, with a non-linear ramp-up across the years.

QIP capex portion of about INR 35 crore is almost fully utilised; the remaining capex spend is expected to complete in the current quarter.
Engineering bench strength being added to support design work on new systems.

demand_pricing: Supply chain is the principal near-term bottleneck: PCB lead times rose from 8-12 weeks to 40-50 weeks; memories, controllers and MLCCs are also short, driven by AI/data-centre demand and Middle East/Europe logistics issues.
Component price increases, higher inventory needs and working capital pressure are flowing through; the company is buying and stocking parts for roughly 12 months of demand.
Q2 BTS margin was held back by a higher material-cost program mix versus last year.

Semiconductor EMS demand is rising almost quarterly for qualified products; the anchor customer is displacing an incumbent operating in Southeast Asia. Management said preliminary talks with other customers are far behind the anchor's traction.

Three new EMS customers: a global tier-1 transport OEM (braking and platform-door controllers, first Indian EMS partner); a German industrial machinery OEM (metrology, first Indian EMS partner); and a Middle East defence customer (drones, design-led, serial orders started, at least USD 10 million per year each once ramped in two to three years).

Global BTS: first Middle East subsystem-level customer and advanced talks with a European customer, both requiring in-country IP. Management said it would sell full systems abroad only after Indian deployment, two to three years away.

Defence exports are targeted at about INR 50,000 crore nationally versus about INR 38,000 crore currently (BTS plus build-to-print). Order mix for the next two to three years expected at about 60% defence and 40% space.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company revise full-year growth guidance given H1 and the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give specific annual guidance, but reiterated a 25-30% medium-term growth target and said visibility is good.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't BTS strength lifted margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said BTS margins are about 20-22% long term and quarterly swings reflect program mix. Q2 had higher material cost in some programs. Company-level margin target is 12.5-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Was BTS Q2 growth a spillover from Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. It reflects higher execution and activity given the larger order book, though quarterly variation is normal, and H2 should be stronger than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity bottlenecks and revenue phasing on the BTS order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No short-term production constraint. Engineering headcount is being added, and a new BTS facility with system-level test infrastructure is planned. Revenue will ramp unevenly over about 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Supply chain constraints (PCB lead times of 40-50 weeks, memory shortages) drove the inventory build. About 50% of net inventory is covered by customer prepayments. INR 50.7 crore of QIP is held as general corporate reserve for future strategic plans.

517569|2026-06.headline: KEI Industries Q1 FY27 net sales rose 23% to INR3,185 crore and operating margin reached 12.43%, with EBITDA up 39.5%.

519003|2026-03.headline: Modi Naturals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% to INR243 crore and PAT 141% to INR19.7 crore, with FY26 PAT up 62.1% to INR50.3 crore.
519003|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to INR243 crore, EBITDA rose 51.8% to INR24.5 crore (10.1% margin) and PAT rose 141% to INR19.7 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 8.5% to INR719 crore, EBITDA grew 31.2% to INR73.5 crore (10.2% margin, excluding exceptional item) and PAT grew 62.1% to INR50.3 crore. Management said the expanded ethanol plant (282 KLPD, up from 130 KL) started commercial operations late in the year, so its contribution was limited in FY26 and is expected to build from FY27. Growth in the consumer and bulk businesses was mixed, with the consumer segment flat for the year and the bulk segment up sharply.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR100 crore (vs INR56.1 crore) and EBITDA INR2.7 crore (vs INR0.9 lakh); FY26 revenue INR198.3 crore (vs INR158.6 crore) and EBITDA INR2.6 crore (vs INR1.7 crore). One solvent extraction plant in Pilibhit was shut for non-viability.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR92.2 crore and EBITDA INR18.5 crore (about 18.8% margin, including an exceptional item); FY26 revenue INR337.4 crore and EBITDA INR58.2 crore (about 17% margin). Management guides about INR950 crore average revenue for FY27 and a sustainable 12-15% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol risk is overcapacity and underutilisation, which management said it is well placed to handle given expansion and tailwinds such as higher blending. Consumer risk is purely execution, given brands and new product lineups.

qa_highlights.question: Is an acquisition in the food sector close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a few food-sector opportunities were evaluated but nothing is firmed up yet; it will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: Will ethanol value-addition revenue show up by end FY27 or early FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one by-product value-added innovation is already helping EBITDA margins and a second is underway, to be completed in a few months; alcohol-side options include potable (RS/ENA, bottling) and downstream chemicals, with little detail shared.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the company of using 282 KLPD, and how long does the PSU OMC order run?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited headroom in consumption and plant location, and said the order covers the ongoing ESY cycle one only, to 31 October 2026, with private OMC registration and tenders expected to add volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ethanol EBITDA margin rise to about 17% from 13% when revenue guidance is INR950 crore, and what is sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the consumer division?

519126|2026-03.headline: HFL posted record FY26 PAT of INR149 crores (+29% YoY) and guides FY27 PAT of INR200-220 crores, while cash flow lagged on working capital.
519126|2026-03.overview: Hindustan Foods delivered record FY26 profitability: total income rose 17% to INR4,264 crores, EBITDA 20% to INR377 crores, and PAT 29% to INR149 crores. Q4 FY26 total income was INR1,120 crores (+17% YoY), EBITDA INR104 crores (+28%), and PAT INR41.5 crores (+32%). Footwear was hit hardest by petrochemical and freight inflation in Q4 and expected to remain affected in Q1 FY27, while pass-through in other verticals continues. Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores but moved the GST inversion-driven shift from gross to net revenue recognition to Q2-Q3 FY27, and withheld sales and segment profitability guidance.

Broke even in Q2 FY26 and said it is PAT positive, but Q4 margins were hit as polymer prices rose ~50-60% and freight rose; pass-through to customers is delayed and Q1 FY27 P&L expected to be affected.

Cone facility acquired and stick facility commissioned; INR50 crore brownfield expansion planned at Lucknow and Panipat.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Record volume growth in the season. New bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27; targets becoming largest independent bottler in India by end FY27, operating as shared manufacturing. INR50 crore investment signed for FY27.

segments.commentary: Steady momentum in FY26. Aurangabad personal care facility integrated from 1 April 2026. Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27. INR50 crore HPC investment signed for FY27. Management cites strong engagement in home care.

segments.commentary: Added customers and completed several domestic and international audits; signed 3-4 new customers for the inherited facility (Baddi, acquired from Reckitt, ~INR220 crore difference between paid and book value). Establishing dedicated ayurvedic wellness facility at Baddi. No revenue or profit figures disclosed.

Target of 20% EBITDA growth and 20% ROE mandated for each of the five verticals.

Gross-to-net revenue recognition shift for some food businesses moved from Q1-Q2 to Q2-Q3 FY27; management says no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT, but margins will look better.

Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27; new beverage bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27.
Baddi ayurvedic wellness facility under establishment, alongside modernisation at the existing Baddi facility; footwear capacity expansion across North and South India.
Management says underutilised assets of about INR508 crores are ramping up; ROCE threshold for new projects is about 18% IRR.
demand_pricing: Footwear polymer prices up roughly 50-60% and freight up; footwear is the only division where raw material pass-through is not immediate. Customers are reportedly supportive.
Most other businesses pass through raw material and packaging cost increases immediately.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear FY26 sales and profitability, and FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales reached about INR500 crores in FY26 and expects INR700-800 crores in FY27. It declined to give a profitability target, citing raw material volatility and ongoing customer talks. CFO said the division broke even in Q2 and is now PAT positive.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block split between dedicated and shared facilities after completing capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Mayank Samdani said the split is about 61% dedicated and 39% shared currently and will stay in a similar range on INR2,150 crores of planned gross block.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment moves to net revenue model and what is the impact on revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said this is mainly food, where packaging and some raw materials carry higher GST. The timeline slipped to Q2-Q3 FY27. Bottom-line EBITDA and PAT are unaffected, but margins will look better as sales fall.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost pressure in footwear not hit FY27 PAT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification across categories should offset footwear headwinds through more than compensatory growth elsewhere. It remains confident in the PAT guidance but cannot yet see how long the uncertainty will last.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise profitability and shared versus dedicated ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined segment EBITDA, promising disclosure by year end, and shared that the gross block by segment is in the presentation. Shared manufacturing targets higher ROCE than dedicated. Dedicated ROE targets are 16-22% pre-tax. Footwear is 100% shared.

qa_highlights.question: Financing of incremental capex given working capital pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said working capital credit has been secured across product lines and is not constraining capex. Net debt to equity is 0.84x with cash buffer, but management will be more cautious and not go all out on investments.

519126|2026-06.headline: Hindustan Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 33% YoY to INR42.8 crore, a record, while footwear cost pressure of ~INR6 crore weighed; FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed.
519126|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 18% YoY to INR1,207 crore and EBITDA rose 26% to INR106.3 crore, with PBT up 33% to INR56.6 crore. Footwear absorbed about INR6 crore of raw material, freight and minimum-wage cost pressure, with the Haryana wage hike the main driver. Management reaffirmed FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore and announced INR190 crore of new projects, taking FY27 commitments to INR340 crore plus INR150 crore carried forward. A Silvassa plant disruption from July rains is expected to be fully resolved by end-August.

financial_highlights.metric: Footwear cost pressure (raw material, freight, wages)

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Running at maximum capacity with a record quarter; Aurangabad personal care integration complete. Silvassa brownfield expected to start in Q2 FY27 and Lucknow greenfield later this year. INR50 crore Lucknow project (bar and liquid lines) announced.

segments.name: Food & Beverages
segments.commentary: Coimbatore, Nashik and Mysuru at record production; beverages had an excellent season. INR210 crore of beverage projects across Coimbatore, Mysuru, Goa, Aurangabad and Hyderabad, expected online by Dec/Jan. Greek yogurt facility being added in Goa.

segments.name: Ice Cream
segments.commentary: Strong summer with record volumes; Panipat facility commissioned in Q1. INR80 crore Panipat expansion announced; Nashik cone and ice cream utilisation improving with new customers.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation was poor due to imported material and freight disruption, and cost pressure hit margins. Management says utilisation is about 80-90% from August; order book full from Q2 FY27 and the business is expected to pay off in H2 FY27. Price pass-through now being achieved from Q1 onward per management.

segments.commentary: Baddi site approved; commercial production started for 2 more multinational companies. Management expects Baddi to reach 100% utilisation within 6-12 months. Class III medical device certification started at Chennai.

519126|2026-09.headline: Hindustan Foods Q2 FY27 adjusted PAT rose 22% YoY to INR46 crore despite a 1.5-month Silvassa flood disruption; FY27 PAT guidance above INR200 crore.

519183|2026-03.headline: ADF Foods Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR196.7 crore (+23.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 17.4%, but Middle East (GCC) exposure clouds FY27 guidance.

519397|2026-03.headline: Sharat Industries FY26 revenue rose about 38% to Rs 524.7 crore and PAT about 60% to Rs 15.90 crore, while Q4 was hit by Middle East disruption and fishmeal costs.
519397|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a strong year on revenue and profit, with export revenue up about 23% and export volumes up about 8%. Q4 revenue grew about 25% YoY to Rs 117.24 crore, but margins were squeezed by the West Asia conflict, which forced rerouting of Middle East-bound shipments, higher logistics costs and inventory build-up, along with sharp fishmeal and soya price increases. US tariffs on Indian shrimp fell from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026, and management is targeting FY27-28 export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore. Management framed the Q4 margin pressure as largely external and event-driven rather than a change in the underlying business.

rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue of more than INR3,200 crore (~INR3,250 crore) with July turnover of ~INR300 crore and quarterly targets of INR840 crore (Q2), INR850 crore (Q3), INR900 crore (Q4), but no upgrade was given and the brief describes the revenue guide as reiterated, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin of 4.6% against ~10% full-year target, air freight of INR12.8-13 cr may persist into Q2 with one customer's 50% recovery not booked, 25% of customers not yet on real-time raw-material settlement, and ~INR10 cr consolidated settlement lag.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CNC machine sales to outside customers started with ~100 machines targeted this year (INR35-40 cr revenue, excluded from guidance), defence shooting ranges with 200 to be supplied this year, and railway supplies started at INR5-7 cr in Q1.

rows.label: Customer price revisions and real-time raw-material settlement
rows.why: About 75% of customers moved to real-time raw-material settlement with the remaining 25% being onboarded, and price increases were sought to offset rupee, labour (Haryana labour cost up ~40%) and power/fuel inflation, which management ties to margin recovery from Q3.

rows.label: Air freight recovery from customer
rows.why: One customer agreed to pay roughly 50% of air freight cost, not yet booked, against Q1 air freight and sorting of about INR12.8-13 crore.

rows.label: Haridwar land sale proceeds
rows.why: About 2 acres held for sale in Haridwar at about INR10 crore expected to be paid in full by 30 December.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR3,250 crore revenue and margin recovery from Q3 but cautious and defensive on Q1 profitability, with evasive answers on air-freight timing and deferred figures on railway revenue, capex and metal impact; analysts pushed on the path to 10% margin, which needs ~12-13

520008|2026-09.headline: Rico Auto Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to negative INR26.3 crore on INR852 crore revenue and INR9.3 crore EBITDA, driven by air freight costs.
520008|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR852 crore and EBITDA was INR9.3 crore, with PAT at negative INR26.3 crore. For H1 FY27, revenue was INR1,607 crore, EBITDA INR46.9 crore and PAT negative INR29.7 crore. Management attributed the weak quarter to West Asia-related shipping disruption that forced air freight on new single-source programs for Toyota and BMW, with air freight cost cited at about INR40 crore. Management said air shipments should end after November 2026 and reiterated an FY27 revenue target of more than INR3,200 crore, while price-increase negotiations with customers are still ongoing.

financial_highlights.change: No YoY or QoQ change stated
No YoY or QoQ change stated
No YoY or QoQ change stated
One-time, per investor question and management reply

segments.name: Aluminium casting
segments.commentary: Contributed 89% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Management said aluminium shipments were on time and had no issues during the quarter.

segments.name: Ferrous (iron) casting
segments.commentary: Contributed about 11% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Management said the heavier iron components drove the freight cost problem, and some light iron components are being moved to other suppliers because they are uneconomic on the company's large machines.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of more than INR3,200 crore, driven by ramp-up of ongoing programs and better utilisation of capacity (implies roughly INR1,593 crore in H2 on H1 of INR1,607 crore).
Air freight expected to end after November 2026; shipping patterns expected to normalise from Q3 with a shift from air to sea freight.
Price-increase negotiations: 2 domestic customers closed, 3-4 more targeted by November end, most customers including BMW (Germany and US) targeted by mid-December 2026.
Management expects a big jump in Q4 FY27 and says price increases and premium freight recovery should be concluded by then.
Management expects at least 10% industry growth next year (FY28), per Mr. Kapur's comments on the domestic market.
capex_capacity: Capacity was expanded to machine more parts in-house to cut dependence on air shipments; management said this added manpower and footprint.
Iron components that are light and uneconomic on large machines are being tagged for transfer to other sources.
Focus stated on transmission, hybrid and EV components for bigger parts; no specific capex amounts or commissioning dates were given.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as strong; management said the company outgrew the industry, with Maruti, Hero and Bajaj cited as growing requirements.
Shipping transit time from India to the US rose from about 5-6 weeks to 10-11 weeks, and Europe transit is similar or longer, pushing up freight cost.
Carbide tooling costs, fuel, aluminium, and labour-driven inflation are not fully passed through; increases are being negotiated, and aluminium prices are now easing.
Two domestic customers have agreed to recover part of the air freight or price increases, and one customer has agreed to contribute toward air freight cost.

qa_highlights.question: Mukesh Mody asked about the long-term strategy to mitigate freight and operating cost volatility, noting INR40 crore paid.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR40 crore was a one-time air freight cost to meet BMW and Toyota commitments, with transit times doubled; it expects zero air shipments after November and is seeking customer recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Bhaskara asked about accountability for the poor quarter and repeated freight issues.
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised, said it was the worst quarter, and blamed new product launches (about 50 launches) and iron-side heavy components; Mr. Verma said a policy will be set to handle such situations earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Kumar asked about the industry outlook over the next 12-18 months.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects commodity prices, especially aluminium, to ease, domestic demand to stay good through Diwali and Q4, and at least 10% growth next year.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Kumar asked about opportunities across PV, CV, hybrid and EV.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is pursuing hybrid and EV work where possible, and continuing ICE, with focus on transmission and larger hybrid/EV components.

risks_watch: Whether air freight truly stops after November 2026 and sea-route transit times normalise from Q3.
Pace of price-increase and freight-recovery closures with customers, especially BMW in Germany and the US, targeted by mid-December.
Q3 and Q4 margin recovery versus the H2 revenue needed to reach the INR3,200 crore target.
Exit of uneconomic light iron components and their effect on revenue and profit.
Shareholder confidence after repeated freight-related losses; a shareholder questioned management credibility and debt levels, which were not answered on the call.
Middle East tensions affecting energy prices, shipping routes and carbide costs.
520008|2026-09.management_tone: Apologetic and defensive on the quarter, with confident forward statements on freight normalisation and Q4 recovery that rest on unconfirmed customer negotiations. Management was evasive on the debt question and did not give specific quantified guidance for margins.
key_quotes: This is a onetime cost that we had to bear because of the chaos that was created.
From November onwards, you will see that most of the containers start reaching there.
And we are determined to get out of this, a lot of learnings that have happened and a lot of corrections have also taken place and a lot of changes that are also taking place.

rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA was INR9.3 crore on INR852 crore revenue (~1.1% margin) after about INR40 crore of air freight; management expects air freight to end after November 2026 and price increases and freight recovery to conclude by Q4, but customer closures are still pending (2 of about 5-7 domestic customers closed).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: In-house machining capacity was added to cut air-freight dependence, but no size, capex or commissioning date was given, so the added capacity is minor and unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management says domestic demand is strong, the company outgrew the industry, and it expects at least 10% industry growth in FY28; FY27 revenue target of more than INR3,200 crore implies roughly INR1,593 crore in H2 versus INR1,607 crore in H1.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue target of more than INR3,200 crore was only held, not raised, and no margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 revenue of about INR1,593 crore is needed to hit the INR3,200 crore target, and H1 PAT was negative INR29.7 crore with price recoveries from BMW and other customers still unconfirmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited about 50 recent launches and a focus on transmission, hybrid and EV components, but no specific product timelines were given.

rows.label: Customer price and air-freight recovery
rows.why: Two domestic customers have closed and 3-4 more are targeted by November end, with BMW and most others by mid-December, but these are still negotiations and not yet signed.

rows.label: Air freight ends; shipping normalises
rows.why: Management expects zero air shipments after November 2026 and a shift to sea freight, against a one-time cost of about INR40 crore in Q2; US transit rose from 5-6 weeks to 10-11 weeks.

rows.label: Q4 FY27 earnings jump
rows.why: Management expects a big jump in Q4 once price increases and premium freight recovery are concluded, though this rests on unconfirmed customer agreements.

tone.note: Management was apologetic and confident on freight normalisation and Q4 recovery, but evasive on the debt question and gave no quantified margin guidance; analysts pressed on accountability, the INR40 crore freight cost, and the credibility of the INR3,200 crore target.

520057|2026-03.headline: JTEKT India FY26 sales grew 11% vs 9% PV market, but full-year EBITDA margin slipped to 7.5% from 7.6% on mix and forex.
520057|2026-03.overview: FY26 sales grew 11% against passenger vehicle market growth of 9%, helped by GST cuts and new Maruti Suzuki models (e Vitara, Victoris). Second-half EBITDA margin recovered to 8.48% from 7.71%, while H1 margin was 6.3%, leaving the full year at 7.5%. Management attributed the margin drag to product mix (Honda down about 33%, 0.33% impact), a forex accounting effect (0.23%) and US tariffs (0.24%), which it called largely temporary. New capacity (CVJ line 2, MS Gear line 5 and 6, CPS line 3) is still under-utilised, and management expects it to reach full utilisation over 1 to 1.5 years. A Brazil export order from the JTEKT group starts dispatch in May 2026.

segments.name: Customer mix FY26
segments.commentary: Maruti Suzuki rose to 60% of sales from 56%, Toyota fell to 10% from 12%, Honda fell to 5% from 8%, M&M and Tata stayed at 10%, exports rose to 3% from 2%.

segments.name: CVJ (driveline)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about INR 130 crore per management; line 2 (from Nov 2025, capacity about 370,000 units) is 27% utilised, line 1 about 83%. Full two-line volume targeted at about INR 250 crore with the Maruti EV MPV from October 2026.

segments.name: Manual gear (MS Gear)
segments.commentary: Line 5 at Dharuhera is at 106% utilisation; line 6 is at 21%, expected to reach 60% then 80-90%. Company holds 40-45% share of manual gear business.

segments.name: CPS
segments.commentary: Line 3 at Bawal is about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.

guidance_outlook: Management expects new capacity to be fully utilised within 1 to 1.5 years, depending on market conditions.

Illustrative FY27 incremental revenue: about INR 400 crore from 10% market growth plus INR 75-100 crore exports, so about INR 500 crore; management referred to INR 800 crore total extra business across FY26 and FY27 (INR 300 crore achieved in FY26). Management declined to give formal FY27 guidance.
Brazil (Stellantis) order to start dispatch in May 2026, about 70,000 units in FY27 (management cited 70,000 this year and 100,000-150,000 next year), with potential to reach 5 lakh units per year.
Honda's EV SUV from Tapukara expected around December 2026, optimistically about 40,000 units and about INR 100 crore business for JTEKT.

Management expects the margin pressures from product mix and forex accounting to be temporary; US tariff reduced from 50% to 10% after the Supreme Court ruling, which management expects to lift US exports.
Capex for FY27 expected to be lower than the last two years; about INR 100 crore more for the Gujarat plant (total committed about INR 250 crore, INR 130 crore spent), plus normal capex.
capex_capacity: CVJ line 2 commissioned November 2025; capacity about 7.54 lakh units per annum (about 3.8 lakh vehicle sets); line 2 utilisation 27%, line 1 about 83%; work started on a third CVJ line.
MS Gear line 5 at Dharuhera 106% utilised; MS Gear line 6 at 21%; MS Gear line 4 at Chennai for export not yet started (SOP pending); capacity about 3.5-4 lakh per MS Gear line.
CPS line 3 at Bawal about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.
Chennai rack and pinion line for Brazil export with installed capacity about 4 lakh units.
Gujarat plant committed at about INR 250 crore; about INR 130 crore spent so far, and about INR 100 crore further spend expected over 1-2 years.
CWIP of about INR 411 crore; management asked analysts to track CWIP as it will weigh on ratios for 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: PV market grew 9% in FY26, with 16.7% growth in H2 after GST cut (28% to 18% for small cars; 50% to 40% for larger ones); H1 growth was only 1.6%.
Honda's passenger vehicle business fell about 30%, reducing JTEKT's sales (almost 100% supplier to Honda); Renault-Nissan export models fell about 16%, Toyota about 4%.
Raw material cost pass-through to customers is back-to-back with a time lag, per management.
Competition in CVJ from GKN-linked and other suppliers, which hold over 60% of Maruti's business; management targets at least 15% CVJ share.
Management said it is not supplying Renault's Duster.

qa_highlights.question: Why have gross margins declined from 29% to 27% over two years, and how should they trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margin was 6.3% and H2 8.48%; net variable cost drag of 0.18% came from a 0.33% mix effect (Honda, Renault-Nissan, Toyota down; Maruti GST-driven models higher), 0.23% forex accounting effect and 0.24% US tariffs, offset by export gains and lower warranty. Management called these temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Has Toyota's Bidadi third line commenced, and what is Toyota's revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bidadi line had not commenced per its understanding; a new Maharashtra facility is expected in H1 FY29, lifting Toyota capacity to about 1 lakh vehicles. JTEKT is the only steering supplier to Toyota.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for other driveline products beyond CVJ and hub bearings for JTEKT's group?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan is finalised; management said it needs 1-1.5 years to stabilise CVJ first. It noted export opportunities for CVJ parts to group entities.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the INR 1,000 crore top-line addition by FY27 and whether revenue can double in 3-4 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 300 crore was added in FY26; with 10% market growth and INR 75-100 crore exports, about INR 500 crore more is possible in FY27 (about INR 800 crore total). It declined to share a formal business plan and said growth depends on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 capex and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex will be lower than the last two years, with about INR 100 crore for Gujarat plus normal capex. ROCE excluding CWIP is above 11%, and full utilisation should push it back toward earlier levels (about 16-17%).

qa_highlights.question: Driveline pipeline, CVJ margins and fixed asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: CVJ margins are better than most MS Gear products and it is 100% localised. Target fixed asset turnover is about 3x overall; CVJ is lower (about 1.5x), CPS 2.5-3x, manual gear 2-2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Potential for exports to US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brazil is the first step, with a Stellantis order, and that a further order could follow once quality and cost are established. No firm US or Europe plan was given.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the H2 run-rate (8.48%) holding and on the forex and mix effects not recurring.
Ramp-up of new capacity: CVJ line 2 at 27% and CPS line 3 at 50% utilisation; delays in the Maruti EV MPV launch (October 2026) and Honda's EV SUV (December 2026) would push out volume.
ROCE at about 10% with CWIP of INR 411 crore; fixed asset turnover has fallen from above 4x to about 2.2x per analyst.
Honda and Renault-Nissan export volume declines; mix shift toward lower-margin Maruti models.
Brazil ramp (70,000 units this year, up to 5 lakh units) and US tariff relief, which were not yet quantified in guidance.
Rising state power tariffs and reciprocal tariffs on US exports.

Confidence is high on the Brazil order and the ramp-up of the Maruti EV programmes, and it deferred on Toyota Bidadi and new product plans.

We expect that whatever capacities we have set up will be 100% utilized over the next 1 year or maybe 1.5 years.

We are currently supplying to 100% of Maruti EV business at this point of time.

rows.why: Brazil Stellantis order starts dispatch May 2026 (about 70,000 units in FY27), Maruti EV MPV with CVJ volume from October 2026, and Honda EV SUV around December 2026 (about 40,000 units, INR 100 crore).

rows.why: ROCE is about 10% with CWIP of INR 411 crore, and management says above 11% excluding CWIP and that full utilisation should push it back toward 16-17%.

520073|2026-03.headline: RACL Geartech FY26 consolidated revenue rose over 20% to ₹512 crore, with Q4 revenue up ~48% YoY to ₹136.69 crore and FY27 guidance of ₹565 crore ±5%.
520073|2026-03.overview: Management reported all-time high FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹512.42 crore (up from ₹425 crore) and consolidated EBITDA of ₹229.16 crore at 25.21% margin. Q4 consolidated revenue was ₹136.69 crore (up ~48% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 24.93% and PBT of ₹16.91 crore. Debt fell to ₹221 crore from ₹297 crore after equity infusion, and debt-equity improved to 0.63x from 1.3x. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ₹565 crore ±5% and a ₹1,000 crore revenue ambition in roughly 3 to 5 years, with a stated aim of reaching it by FY29 if possible.

segments.name: Geography (FY26)
segments.commentary: Exports ~75% of turnover (Europe ~69%, Asia Pacific and India ~29%, US and Canada ~2%); export turnover ₹346.68 crore consolidated, domestic ₹110 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Per-kit value not disclosed. Assemblies not currently demanded by RE, though RACL supplies full gearboxes to TVS and KTM and has the capability.

qa_highlights.question: Why can growth not exceed 20% given recovery from Europe and KTM issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20% on ₹500 crore adds ₹100 crore in absolute terms; growth is constrained by capital intensity, lead times and quality of ramp-up, so it targets sustainable growth.

qa_highlights.question: Capex needed beyond FY27 for a ₹1,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex beyond FY27 will be disclosed once documents are ready; Crystal will require significant additional investment.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to US tariffs, European demand slowdown and currency risk?
qa_highlights.answer: US dollar exports are only 2-3%; exports go via EU, Mexico and Canada. No slowdown seen; rupee depreciation helps partly offset inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue not disclosed; management said about 10,000-20,000 motorcycles could run on the parts if demand is met.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 gross margin lower and is guidance being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some expenses shift between Q3 and Q4; no revision to FY27 guidance, which retains ±5% flexibility.

Capex needs for Project Crystal and the ₹1,000 crore ambition; debt funding will follow assured business.
Q4 gross margin softness and quarterly expense timing; watch the first carbon disclosure promised from next quarter.
Shift drum and Crystal validations; ZF order recovery after a weak FY26.

520111|2026-09.headline: Ratnamani Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR1,348 crores, but EBITDA margin was 16.3% amid elevated freight costs; standalone order book above INR2,600 crores.
520111|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR1,348 crores, with EBITDA of INR220 crores (16.3% margin) and PAT of INR133 crores. Standalone revenue grew 18% to INR1,104 crores, with EBITDA margin at 12.6%, and the standalone business remains debt-free. Management attributed margin pressure to sharply higher ocean freight, duty and local transport costs on DDP-basis US exports under a 50% tariff, and to lower domestic demand and utilisation. The order book rose about 30% QoQ to over INR2,600 crores, with stainless steel near INR1,000 crores and carbon steel near INR1,700 crores. Management held FY27 standalone guidance of INR4,000-4,200 crores and consolidated guidance of INR5,000-5,200 crores.

RFSS expansion partly commissioned; induction bend production expected to start next quarter (Q3 FY27).
RFSS full potential revenue INR1,200-1,500 crores at 4,000 tonnes capacity; realisation roughly INR2,500-3,500 per kg, depending on material.

qa_highlights.answer: Existing orders are fixed-price and cannot be repriced; future orders are being priced to reflect costs; detention and demurrage charges under discussion.

521016|2026-03.headline: Indo Count guides FY27 revenue to about INR5,500 crore (over 30% growth) and EBITDA margin to about 13%, versus 11% in FY26.
521016|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue was flat at about INR4,211 crore (total income) versus INR4,191 crore in FY25, but EBITDA fell to INR461 crore (11% margin) from INR577 crore (13.8%) on new-business incubation costs, lower fixed-cost absorption and case-by-case tariff sharing. Q4 FY26 total income rose to INR1,088 crore (QoQ from INR1,074 crore), with EBITDA of INR116 crore (10.7% margin) and PAT of INR24 crore. Core business fell by a low-teens percentage in FY26 on U.S. tariff volatility, while new business revenue reached INR792 crore. Management guided FY27 to a record year with volumes of 105-110 million meters (FY26: 94 million) and consolidated revenue of about INR5,500 crore.

financial_highlights.change: +6% YoY; vs INR1,074 crore in Q3 FY26
+22% YoY (margin 9.3% in Q4 FY25); +14% QoQ (margin 9.5% in Q3 FY26)
+15% YoY vs INR21 crore; similar to Q3 FY26
down about INR200 crore from INR960 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR792 crore (about USD270 million per the call's INR270 crore figure for the quarter)

segments.name: Core business
segments.commentary: Core business declined by a low-teens percentage in FY26 due to U.S. tariffs; non-U.S. share was about 30% of core revenue, with FY27 non-U.S. growth guided at 20%. Core FY27 revenue guided at about INR4,000 crore, with core EBITDA margin targeted at about 15%.

segments.name: New business (utility bedding and U.S. brands)
segments.commentary: New business revenue was INR792 crore in FY26, split about 2/3 utility bedding and 1/3 brands, and is guided to about INR1,500 crore in FY27. Management said new business is now EBITDA positive, with utility bedding targeted at 15% margin and brands at 100-200 bps above core margin.

segments.name: U.S. utility bedding
segments.commentary: Three U.S. facilities now produce 31 million pillows and 1.5 million quilts per year (up from 13 million pillows). The two older facilities run at about 65% utilisation, with 60-65% across all three targeted in FY27; management said this level is EBITDA positive.

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Domestic business under brands Boutique Clothing and Layers contributed about 2.25% of FY26 revenue, with about 2,000 touch points.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of about INR5,500 crore, growth of over 30%; incremental revenue of about INR1,300 crore, of which core about INR4,000 crore and new business about INR1,500 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin target of around 13%, including other income; management said core business is kept at about 15% in this guidance.
FY27 volume guidance of 105-110 million meters versus 94.1 million meters in FY26.
Non-U.S. core revenue expected to grow 20% in FY27.
Target of about USD275 million (about INR2,500 crore) in new business by 2028 and revenue doubling by 2028 over the FY25 base (about INR8,000 crore run rate, stated as sometime in calendar 2028).
Capex outlay of INR250 crore over the next 12-18 months, funded 75% internal accruals and 25% debt; long-term debt repayment of about INR85-90 crore a year for the next couple of years.
Tax rate of 25%; no change expected in interest profile or effective tax rate.
Company expects to pass on raw material cost increases to customers within about a quarter.
capex_capacity: U.S. utility bedding: North Carolina greenfield facility commenced operations in FY26, taking U.S. facilities to three with capacity of 31 million pillows and 1.5 million quilts per year (from 13 million pillows).
Existing two U.S. utility bedding facilities at about 65% utilisation; overall 60-65% utilisation across three facilities targeted in FY27.
Planned capex of INR250 crore over 12-18 months, to be funded by internal accruals and debt; management said the company has largely completed its planned growth investments.
Cotton sourcing: about 70% domestic and 30% imported (Egyptian and American extra-long staple); import share expected to stay around 30%.
demand_pricing: No customer loss or order cancellations in FY26, per management; some tariff impact was absorbed to protect share.

Orders are placed about 60 days ahead; customers planned around 50% U.S. tariff until mid-February 2026, when it reduced to 10%, causing Q4 volume weakness (20.5 million meters vs about 24-25 million in earlier quarters).
U.S. retailers have raised retail prices and consumers have accepted them; management said there is no restocking and sales flow is at normalised levels.
Q4 realisations rose on forex gains and a more favourable product mix; management said product mix is normalising after prior down-trading.

Raw material cost inflation (cotton, yarn, polyester, dyes, chemicals, energy, packaging) over the last 30-60 days; repricing with customers is in progress. Indian cotton import duty waiver notified recently, which management said levels the playing field for Indian sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and debt evolve over the next four quarters given tariff relief, a weaker INR and higher cotton prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 13% margin guidance, citing recent raw material inflation that will be passed on through repricing. Long-term debt repayment is INR85-90 crore a year; the INR250 crore capex is 75% internally funded and 25% debt-funded.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 revenue guidance backed by visibility, and why does new business double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is at about INR1,100 crore run rate, with Q4 new business at about INR270 crore; it cited business visibility, with no specific pipeline numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Will utility bedding reach EBITDA breakeven, and when will the greenfield facility do so?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer reports by facility. At 60-65% utilisation on 31 million pillows, the segment is EBITDA positive; the 150-200 bps launch drag ends from Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin guide only 13% when the company historically earned 15-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Core business is kept at about 15% in guidance; new business was previously a drag but is now EBITDA positive, so it is expected to add to margins gradually. Management declined to comment on Q4 FY27 margin exit rate.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 doubling-of-revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the target of about INR8,000 crore run rate by 2028 (calendar year), not within FY27-28, and declined to give more detail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effect of the Indian cotton import duty waiver, and what will the import mix be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30% of raw material is imported (long/extra-long staple, exempt from duty already); the waiver levels the field for domestic cotton, and the import share is expected to stay near 30%.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (cotton, polyester, energy, packaging) and the speed of repricing with U.S. customers; management said a lag effect is possible.
Dependence on U.S. tariff levels: the 50% tariff through mid-February 2026 drove Q4 volumes down; future tariff or trade-deal changes could shift demand.
Utility bedding and brand ramp-up: utilisation must reach 60-65% across three U.S. facilities for the EBITDA-positive claim; Wamsutta revenue is still small and undisclosed.
Other income (about INR30 crore in Q4) is largely forex-driven and may not be sustained, per the call's own discussion.

Working capital: management said incremental revenue would come at about 120 days working capital, so the FY27 revenue jump requires substantial funding; floating-rate debt exposed to interest rate changes.
Management declined to comment on quarterly trajectory (Q1 FY27 versus Q4) and on the Q4 FY27 margin exit rate.
521016|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story and the FY27 record-year guidance, but cautious and terse on specifics: management declined to give facility-level data, quarterly guidance, or the Q4 FY27 margin exit rate, and repeatedly stated the FY28 target as a run rate for calendar 2028 rather than a fiscal-year target.
key_quotes: Simply put, we are on track to deliver a record year in FY27.
We would not be -- I mean, very difficult to comment on that at this point of time.
So, there's no overhang of what we have mentioned in the previous years that we have taken a brunt of 150 to 200 basis points to launch these new businesses.
I think it will remain at 30%. We don't see any much big change.

rows.why: Management is confident on FY27 record year, but Q4 volumes were weak at 20.5 million meters and tariff relief from mid-Feb 2026 is a tailwind only if demand recovers; no explicit upgrade signalled.

rows.why: Raw material inflation (cotton, yarn, polyester, energy) with repricing lag, US tariff volatility, and other income (~INR30 crore in Q4, forex-driven) may not be sustained; management declined to comment on Q1 FY27 trajectory or Q4 FY27 margin exit.

521016|2026-06.headline: Indo Count Q1 FY27 total income rose 13% QoQ to INR1,224 crore and EBITDA margin recovered to 13.1%, with volumes up 12% QoQ.
521016|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with total income of INR1,224 crore (+13% QoQ, +27% YoY) and EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% QoQ) at a 13.1% margin. Sales volume rose 12% QoQ to 23 million meters but fell 3% YoY on container shortages linked to the West Asia conflict. The new business (utility bedding and US brands) reached INR387 crore in the quarter. Bhilad plant was hit by flooding from 23 July 2026 and only partially resumed on 12 August 2026; the company says it is fully insured.

financial_highlights.change: Nearly tripled over past one year (per management)
vs INR80 crore last year (per management)
Q4 FY26 included one-off ~INR13 crore GST-related hit

segments.name: Core business (bed linen, quilts, comforters etc.)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR837 crore, +4% QoQ; ~70% US and ~30% non-US. Management says core blended margin is around 15%, with standalone margin slightly above 15% in Q1. Quarterly realisation fell on product mix.

segments.name: New business (utility bedding + US brands)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR387 crore in Q1, all US-linked. Split is roughly two-thirds utility bedding (manufacturing) and one-third brands; brand revenue was slightly above INR125 crore. FY27 target INR1,500 crore; brands target about INR500 crore for the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance reiterated at 105-110 million meters; core business revenue about INR4,000 crore.
FY27 new business revenue target INR1,500 crore; USD275 million new business ambition for 2028 and INR8,000 crore revenue aspiration by CY2028 reiterated.
Non-US revenue expected to grow 20%+ in FY27.
Endeavour to maintain about 13% blended EBITDA margin for FY27 on a consolidated basis; long-term stabilisation target 15-16% for the company as a whole.
Price increases concluded with customers; impact on realisations expected from Q2 onwards. Full-year realisations expected broadly intact.
Interest cost expected at about INR120 crore for FY27 (INR30 crore per quarter), at roughly 6-7%.
Utility bedding utilisation targeted at 60-65% for FY27.
Potential US tariff refund: management expects no material financial benefit; ~80% of exports are FOB; quantification premature, clarity expected by year-end.
capex_capacity: New greenfield facility in North Carolina commenced in January 2026; operations ramping, adding employee costs and a lower-margin gestation period.
Existing US facilities in Ohio and Arizona; utilisation overall around 60-65% in Q1 despite new capacity.

Bhilad (Gujarat) plant hit by flooding from 23 July 2026; partially resumed 12 August 2026 with phased normalisation. Management says other plants are absorbing lost output (endeavour, not confirmed).
Utility bedding business investment about 70-75% complete per management, with balancing investments still to come.
demand_pricing: Volumes recovering as US tariff uncertainty eased; Q1 seen as seasonally softer than Q2 and Q3 (US festive period).
Container availability constraints from the West Asia conflict hit Q1 dispatches; management says the container issue continues.
Raw material costs rose after the February-end war; price increases were negotiated case by case and concluded, with impact from Q2.
Non-US: UK FTA restores level playing field (UK business 8-10% of total); management says client interactions in UK rose from about 4 to 8 a year. EU FTA expected to add further duty-free access.
Competition: India at about 10% US tariff vs neighbours at 10-12.5%; management says no orders or customers were lost even at 50% tariff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference between core bed linen and the new utility bedding and branded businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15% for both bed linen and utility bedding over time, and brands 100-200 bps above that. Utility bedding is currently lower because the new facility is in gestation; bed linen did slightly better than 15% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is any US tariff refund expected and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff refund was booked in Q1. Management expects no material benefit as ~80% of exports are FOB, and says quantification is premature until year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone margins decline in Q2 and Q3 given Bhilad disruption and cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined precise quarterly guidance; the endeavour is to hold about 13% blended consolidated margin for the full year. Any one-time losses are covered by insurance (property, inventory, loss of profit).

qa_highlights.question: Why is utility bedding utilisation guided at only 60-65% when Q1 already achieved that?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-65% is the satisfactory level to plan on for the full year, with stability expected for the rest of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost run-rate and weighted average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost is about INR30 crore per quarter (INR120 crore annual); the Q4 figure included a one-off ~INR13 crore GST-related charge. Cost is roughly 6-7%, varying by bank; company rated A1+.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins go beyond 15% long term given the shift to branded and e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: No ceiling is set. Long-term target is to stabilise at 15-16% for the company as a whole, to be recalibrated as the business progresses.

risks_watch: Bhilad plant recovery pace after flooding; whether lost output is made up in Q2-Q3 without delays in shipments.
Container availability and West Asia-linked freight constraints, which cut Q1 volumes 3% YoY.
Quarterly realisation pressure from product mix; price increases on raw material costs to flow through from Q2.
Utility bedding: non-cotton input cost inflation, and whether it is fully passed on (management says yes, with 2-3 month lag at times).
New business ramp: management says variability is still unknown and about 70-75% of the investment is in place; USD100 million brand target is three years out.
Potential US tariff refund accounting, with clarity expected only by year-end.

rows.why: Bhilad plant only partially resumed on 12 Aug 2026 after 23 July flooding, container shortages continue, and the 3% YoY Q1 volume decline makes the 105-110 mn m target depend on a strong H2 catch-up.

rows.why: Management guides non-US revenue up 20%+ in FY27; UK business is 8-10% of total and UK client interactions rose from about 4 to 8 a year after the UK FTA.

rows.label: New business INR1,500 crore FY27 target
rows.why: New business revenue was INR387 crore in Q1 (run-rate ~INR1,550 crore annualised) and target is held, but ramp variability is still unknown and utility bedding utilisation is targeted at only 60-65%.

rows.why: Management expects no material financial benefit as ~80% of exports are FOB, and no refund was booked in Q1.

521016|2026-09.headline: Indo Count Q2 FY27 total income rose 57% YoY to INR1,699 crore and EBITDA margin hit 15.3%, with H1 margin 14.4% above the 13% full-year guidance.
521016|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarter, with total income of INR1,699 crore (up 57% YoY, 39% QoQ) and EBITDA more than doubling to INR259 crore. PAT rose to INR132 crore from INR39 crore. Net debt fell to INR518 crore, the lowest level, and net debt to equity was 0.2x. Management said it expects to exceed FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance, but did not raise the numeric guidance, and reiterated the CY28 revenue target of INR8,000 crore.

financial_highlights.change: +57% YoY, +39% QoQ vs INR1,082 crore in Q2 FY26
vs INR123 crore; margin +380 bps YoY
vs INR39 crore in Q2 FY26 (about 2.5x)
+42% vs INR2,049 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR518 crore; net debt to equity 0.2x
financial_highlights.change: lowest ever; cash INR315 crore vs INR114 crore at March 2026

financial_highlights.value: INR45 crore 2 lakh net of salvage
financial_highlights.change: offset by equal insurance claim booked as exceptional item; interim insurance payment INR14 crore 99 lakh approved after quarter end

segments.name: Core bed linen
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR2,033 crore, about 50% of the INR4,000 crore FY27 target. Core EBITDA is above the ~15% guided level; about 70% of core revenue is US and 30% non-US.

segments.name: New businesses (utility bedding, branded, other home textiles)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR502 crore (~30% of total income); H1 revenue INR890 crore, nearly 60% of the INR1,500 crore FY27 target. Mix is roughly two-thirds utility bedding and one-third branded. EBITDA margin is in the low double digits, below core, and is expected to reach core levels (~15%) at full utilisation.

segments.name: US utility bedding plants
segments.commentary: All three US facilities have ramped up and are running at over 65% utilisation, with management saying all three are above 65%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance of 105-110 million meters volume, INR5,500 crore total income and 13% EBITDA margin: management expects to exceed both the revenue and EBITDA guidance. H1 delivered 51 million meters (~49% of volume guidance) and INR2,923 crore (~53% of revenue guidance).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance may move from 13% to 14-15%, but management said it will not go beyond that. It declined to change guidance to 18-20%.

CY28 target of doubling revenue from FY25 to INR8,000 crore (branded business target $100 million by CY28); management reiterated this and said it does not need growth capex to reach it. Management will provide next-year guidance later.
Non-US core revenue is expected to grow over 20% in FY27; the non-US share of core could move from about 30% toward 40-50% over the next few years, though management gave no firm number.

FY27 capex guidance of INR250 crore is to be spent over 12-18 months, with about INR40 crore spent in H1; the full amount will not be spent this year. Spinning capex is mostly expected by year-end, and effluent treatment will likely spill into FY28.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance of INR250 crore over 12-18 months; about INR40 crore spent in H1 FY27.
Projects: spinning (mostly expected to complete before FY27 year-end) and effluent treatment plant (likely to spill over into FY28).

Core business utilisation is about 73%, with some spare capacity; board to decide on further capex at an appropriate time. Management said no growth capex is needed to reach the CY28 INR8,000 crore target.
All three US utility bedding plants above 65% utilisation; management targets full utilisation of the utility business by CY28.
demand_pricing: Average realisation rose sharply, which management attributed to higher-value orders executed this quarter and product mix; management said the mix is sustainable. Refunds of US tariffs are not included in the realisation gain.
Gross margin is expected to range 50-55% on an annualised basis and should not be judged quarter by quarter, due to product mix.

Cotton and cotton-related input costs have risen; the company holds 4-5 months of inventory as a cushion and passes on increases with a lag of one to two quarters. Management said the previous input cost increase has been fully passed on and sees no margin pressure.
Freight is largely on FOB or CIF terms, so customers bear freight hikes.
UK FTA implemented in July 2026; EU FTA not yet effective. Customer inquiries are rising in the UK and EU, and management said the UK and EU addressable opportunity is comparable to the US.
Wamsutta expanded into broader US retail, and was a major driver of branded growth. Growth came from both market share gains and wallet share gains with existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Do margins already reflect rising input costs, or is there downside ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cotton inputs are covered by 4-5 months of inventory and price increases are passed on with a one-to-two-quarter lag, so no margin pressure is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company double its size from FY27 to FY30 and reach INR10,000 crore at 20% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stays with the CY28 guidance of doubling revenue from FY25 to INR8,000 crore and will give next-year guidance later. It said it will work towards more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between core and new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Core EBITDA is about 15% and above that in Q2. New businesses are in the low double digits and should reach core levels within the next two to three quarters, with full utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Has US core volume recovered to FY25 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY25 volume was about 106 million meters and FY27 is heading to roughly the same level, with US and non-US combined to recover the base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the working capital cycle improved from March, with the number of days down by at least three weeks as of 30 September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 capex of INR250 crore be fully spent this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The INR250 crore is over 12-18 months; about INR40 crore was spent in H1, with spinning mostly done this year and effluent treatment spilling into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Could margin guidance move to 18-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Not immediately. The FY27 margin could go from 13% to 14-15%, but management said it will not go beyond that.

risks_watch: US demand and operating environment after the midterm elections; management declined to comment on the results and said the order book is healthy.
Input cost (cotton and yarn) inflation and the timing of pass-through to customers.
New business margins are still in the low double digits; reaching the ~15% core level depends on utilisation and the branded mix.
Bhilad flood: final insurance settlement is pending (interim INR14 crore 99 lakh received approval); the INR45 crore inventory loss is offset as an exceptional item.
Dependence on US volumes: the non-US share of core is only about 30% today, and EU FTA timing is uncertain.
Management gave no numeric guidance beyond FY27 and CY28, and no split of the remaining capex between H2 FY27 and FY28.

It was cautious on numeric upgrades, holding guidance and limiting the margin raise to 14-15%. It deflected or declined on several specifics, including the midterm election impact, the non-US mix, the capex split, and the cost bridge.
key_quotes: Continuing with the Q1 momentum, we have delivered our highest -ever quarterly performance in Q2.
Overall, the blended margin for this year, we have guided it, given in 13%. Overall, we should be exceeding that.
The full INR250 crores will not be spent during this year.
Gross margin should be looked at on annual basis. Do not go with quarter- by- quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spinning capacity expansion mostly complete by FY27 year-end and effluent treatment plant spilling into FY28, but these are minor adds and management said no growth capex is needed to reach CY28 INR8,000 crore target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 volume 51 million meters is ~49% of the 105-110 million meter FY27 guide; FY27 heading to roughly FY25's ~106 million meters, and US utility plants are all above 65% utilisation with new businesses ramping.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Core utilisation is about 73% with spare capacity, management says no growth capex is needed for the CY28 INR8,000 crore target, and FY27 capex of INR250 crore is being deferred over 12-18 months with only INR40 crore spent in H1.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it expects to exceed FY27 revenue guidance above INR5,500 crore (H1 is INR2,923 crore, ~53%) and raised the margin guide to 14-15%, though it declined to change the numeric guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue is already ~53% of the INR5,500 crore guide and EBITDA margin is 14.4%, with cotton cost increases passed on with a 1-2 quarter lag and no margin pressure expected by management.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Branded growth via Wamsutta broader US retail and UK FTA (effective July 2026) with rising UK/EU inquiries, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: UK FTA and EU opportunity

Working capital days rose from 169 to 184 and operating cash flow was negative on a standalone basis, which management attributed to heavy dispatches in the last two months of the year. Several large orders slipped by about a quarter due to the Middle East crisis, and the Monga Strayfield dispatches were delayed by logistics constraints.

Order inflow was about INR134-135 crores in the quarter and about INR190 crores year-to-date, against an internal group target of INR800 crores for FY27. Management also said the equity fundraise is complete and the balance sheet is net debt-free.

qa_highlights.answer: Amritanshu Khaitan said proceeds strengthen the balance sheet (net debt-free) and partly fund capex to support over INR1,000 crores revenue; acquisitions are being evaluated but none announced; no further fundraise needed.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in reaching INR800 crore order inflow with 9 months left, and Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR4,000 crore inquiry pipeline and fertilizer traction; no current Middle East orders, but a couple of large inquiries were at final commercial stage before the conflict, now on hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why revenue growth ambition of about 25% has slipped to about 10-12% and what is being done differently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited customer-side dependencies, nuclear approvals taking longer than private jobs, and greenfield projects held by environmental clearances; no FY28 guidance until order booking through March 2027 is clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure linked to Kilburn standalone weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said the company has consistently maintained 20%+ margins on a consolidated basis, citing cost and execution discipline, and reports consolidated because of cross-selling.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and working capital status?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said collections were received after March; debtors and net working capital have not changed substantially but are better than the March quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why were two managers (Nitin Varadkar, Dinesh Nikam) designated senior management personnel?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Lala said it is a SEBI LODR disclosure requirement for reporting lines one level below the CEO after recent promotions; no board induction planned.

522113|2026-03.headline: Timken India Q4 FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for first time, up 14.2% YoY to INR10,731 million; PBT margin 19.3%.
522113|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue from operations was INR10,731 million (up 14.2% YoY), the first quarter above INR1,000 crore, with PBT of INR2,074 million (19.3% margin) after a labour code impact. FY26 standalone revenue hit a record INR31,478 million (up 8.6%), with PBT of INR5,304 million (up about 3%) and PBT margin of 15.5%. The Board approved merging Timken GGB into Timken India. Management flagged input cost inflation entering FY27, with price pass-through only about 10% achieved so far, and said the new Bharuch plant is ramping slowly with about INR80 crore of FY26 revenue.

Price increases to offset raw material inflation (steel, grinding wheels, coolants, currency): about 10% achieved as of the call, with the aim of completing most of the pass-through over the current and next quarter.

Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR120 crore capex): first production targeted for November-December 2026, with asset turns of about 2x to start.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of revenue (management pegged last two years at about 8.5%), covering Jamshedpur rail, GGB plain bearings at Bharuch and some heat-treatment investment.
Management said the 65:35 domestic-manufactured to imported mix may hold for the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bharuch new plant: all lines capitalised; smaller lines and spherical lines running near full, large-line PPAPs under way, and CRB lines running close to two shifts. More than 100 new part introductions underway. FY26 revenue from the plant about INR80 crore (Q4 about INR60 crore, Q3 about INR12 crore). Management said the plant is still close to breakeven.

Bharuch total investment about INR720 crore including forex; buildings about INR350 crore; plant and machinery roughly INR310-320 crore by management's estimate. Peak revenue said to be close to 2x asset turns, but management ruled out INR1,000 crore.

Capital is debt-free; management said it will consider further expansion (0-8 inch range for CV and tractors, M&A) if the project is right.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is stable across most segments and is not among its top three concerns; cost escalation and pass-through, Bharuch ramp-up/PPAP, and expansion projects are the top three.
Steel MRO is slow and steel melt was lower in the quarter; cement MRO is good. OE sentiment is wait-and-watch because of geopolitics.
North America export demand is gaining momentum even without a signed US trade deal; the US is about 50% of exports, per the analyst.
CV demand described as robust with cyclicality; tractors okay; rail slow and steady; aftermarket okay.
Pricing: price increases began mid-April 2026 for both pass-through and recovery; about 10% realised, with automotive customers expected to delay. Management hopes for retrospective recovery.
Management said the Indian bearing market is about USD 2-2.5 billion (about 65% mobile, 35% stationary) and expects process and distribution to grow fastest.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken to offset raw material inflation, and will there be margin pressure in the next 1-2 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Price pass-through has only begun, at about 10%; management expects the rest over the current and next quarter, with the automotive OEM segment lagging. Management did not quantify the margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for domestic rail, CV, and US exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 exports were INR222 crore (up about 40% QoQ, up about 66% YoY for the full year); rail was INR278 crore in Q4 (slight YoY decline); CV described as robust.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch utilisation targets and FY26 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue about INR80 crore; utilisation expected to reach about 70% by July-August 2026, then improve monthly.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4: rail 26%, mobile others 19%, distribution 15%, process 19%, exports 21% (total INR1,073 crore including intercompany). FY26 total INR3,419 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Jamshedpur capex timeline and asset turns; FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Production targeted for November-December 2026 at about 2x asset turns to start. FY27 capex expected at 8-10% of revenue; no formal capex guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend level?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY26 final dividend was INR2.5 per share on INR10 face value, down from INR36 previously. Management said it pays large dividends every 3-4 years and will consider the shareholder's request.

522113|2026-06.headline: Timken India Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~15% YoY to INR929 crore, with PBT of INR150 crore and PBT margin of 16.2%.
522113|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR929 crore, up almost 15% YoY, after a seasonally strong Q4 FY26 (highest standalone revenue of INR3,147 crore for FY26). PBT rose to INR150 crore from INR130 crore, with PBT margin at 16.2% versus 16.1% a year earlier, and EBITDA margin at 19.6%. Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to heavy-truck and off-highway price increases offsetting unfavourable Q1 mix. The Bharuch plant is ramping up quickly, with revenue of about INR50 crore in the quarter and near breakeven.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR200 crore, about 22% of Q1 revenue. Management described government railway buying as slow and sluggish, and said the year started with about 3% growth in rail.

segments.name: Mobile / others
segments.commentary: INR184 crore. Management said mobile (tractors, heavy trucks) is about 20% of the business and is where price increases are sticking.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR153.9 crore (about INR154 crore).

segments.name: Process
segments.commentary: INR186 crore, up about 28-30% YoY, driven by metals customers and wind (gearbox exports and domestic wind farms).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR200 crore, including about 1% export incentive. Intercompany push to America rose about 21%; Europe is down, China and ASEAN are down, and the US is up.

segments.name: Bharuch plant (within segments)
segments.commentary: About INR50 crore revenue in Q1, close to breakeven. Spherical roller bearing (SRB) line utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, targeted at about 70% by August-September; CRB line utilisation is lower, with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

guidance_outlook: Bharuch SRB line expected to reach about 70% utilisation in August-September 2026; CRB line ramp toward end of Q2 and Q3.
Rail expansion at Jamshedpur expected to start commercial production by calendar year-end 2026; management said it will ramp up immediately after that.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of sales, with project work described as on track; timing may spill some capex into FY28.
Further cost escalation seen as limited beyond the steel, carbide, coal and grinding increases already in the system; base oil described as the only volatile input.
Management said it will continue to pass on cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew; rail and PSU/ARC contracts are fixed and will reprice only at renewal.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramping up; three manufacturing lines; utilisation cannot be given at plant level but SRB demand is higher than CRB at this stage.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur on track; plain bearings investment at Bharuch on track.
Manufactured vs traded mix roughly 75/25, similar to prior quarters.
Gas conversion from LPG to natural gas completed across supply chain and plants.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven by resilient core-segment demand and both export and domestic execution.
Steel producers raised prices by about INR1,500-1,600 per tonne in January and about INR3,500 per tonne by April, around INR5,000 per tonne in total; most customers have started paying the increase.
Price pass-through is working in heavy truck and tractor/off-highway; rail, PSU and cement customers are on fixed annual rate contracts.
Process growth partly from metals projects (mills built in India for export) and wind.
Management said the US market is up, Europe and China are down, and ASEAN and Australia are flat to down.
No direct tariff figure given; management said the US landed tariff has moved over time and it would confirm the current rate.
Management said the parent's 80/20 portfolio review is aimed at performance improvement; no change in Indian strategy was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail INR200 crore (22%), mobile/others INR184 crore, distribution INR153.9 crore, process INR186 crore, exports about INR200 crore including 1% export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of parent's 80/20 strategy and belts divestment on India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80/20 is a Pareto-based performance tool that is being applied globally; it is not yet a change in strategy for India. The India focus stays on off-highway, rail and tractor/heavy-truck, with no two-wheeler, passenger car or washing-machine ball bearings.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch ramp-up and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Bharuch revenue was about INR50 crore, close to breakeven. SRB utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, expected to reach about 70% by August-September; CRB is lower with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of process and export growth and US outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Process grew about 30% YoY, from metals and wind. Exports to the US are growing, Europe is down, and the intercompany push to America is about 21%.

qa_highlights.question: Rail outlook and Jamshedpur ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Government railway procurement is slow due to funds diverted to infrastructure and defence; management expects this to be timing-related. Jamshedpur rail capacity is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation has been passed through to price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to give an exact percentage; heavy truck and tractor customers have largely passed through cost escalation, while rail and PSU contracts will reprice at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex plan and allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-wise split not given; capex directionally in line with the 8-10% of sales range, with some timing spillover into the next fiscal.

522113|2026-09.headline: Timken India Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 25.4% YoY to INR 969 crore, with PBT up 29.5% to INR 156 crore and PBT margin at 16.1%.

522163|2026-06.headline: Diamond Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 129% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT rose 191% to INR58.5 crores, with FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crores.
522163|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR690 crores (up 129% YoY), EBITDA INR85 crores (12.3% margin, up ~200 bps) and PAT INR58.5 crores (8.5% margin). Management attributed the quarter's softness versus a normal Q1 to early, heavy monsoon flooding in Gujarat that hit medium and extra high voltage cable laying. The company completed a INR1,640 crore QIP (net INR1,614 crore), turning net worth positive at INR691 crore post-QIP from negative INR922 crore at June 30, 2026. Order book stood at INR3,688 crore as on August 11, 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore and FY28 of INR7,500 crore.

segments.commentary: Currently negligible. Team being built; certifications for Europe and US in progress. Internal target of INR500 crore export order book by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery expectation on the INR957 crore legacy receivables.
